definition_zh: 行政的；管理的；政务的；（处罚等）由行政机关作出的
definition_en: relating to the management of an organization, the work of government, or decisions made by officials rather than courts
core_image: 一张盖着公章的文件，把决定从桌面推向整个机构
scene: 新校区启用前，各种审批、报表与人事手续堆满了办公桌。Most of the delay came from administrative work rather than from teaching.
sceneCN: 这里 administrative 表示「文书事务的」（第 3 个义项：日常办公事务）；句意为延误多半出在行政事务上，而不是教学。

derivatives.zh: 由 administrate 加 -or 构成，义为「管理者、行政人员」
由 administrate 加 -tion 构成，义为「管理、行政部门」
由本词去掉形容词后缀构成，义为「管理、实施」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在行政上」

senses.title: Relating to the running of an organization
senses.definition: concerned with managing the daily affairs of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 与组织日常事务的管理有关
senses.example: She took on the administrative side of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她接手了这个项目的管理工作。
senses.why: The adjective describes whatever belongs to administrare, the work of managing or serving an organization.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述一切属于 administrare 的工作，也就是为组织做管理或服务。

senses.title: Relating to government
senses.definition: concerned with the work of government and its officials
senses.definitionCN: 与政府及其官员的工作有关
senses.example: The region has its own administrative status.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区有自己的行政地位。
senses.why: A government is the largest body that administers a territory, so the word naturally covers public rule.
senses.whyCN: 政府是管辖一片土地的最大机构，所以这个词自然覆盖公共治理。

senses.title: Relating to paperwork and routine office work
senses.titleCN: 文书事务的；日常办公的
senses.definition: concerned with records, forms, and routine office procedures rather than policy
senses.definitionCN: 与记录、表格和日常办公流程有关，而非政策本身
senses.example: Most of the delay came from administrative work rather than from teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 延误多半出在行政事务上，而不是教学。
senses.why: Administration in practice means files and forms, so the adjective marks that everyday layer of work.
senses.whyCN: 实际的管理工作就是文件和表格，这个形容词标出的正是这一层日常事务。

senses.title: Decided by an official body rather than a court
senses.definition: imposed or handled by an authority or official rather than by a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 由当局或官员施加、处理，而非由法院处理
senses.example: He was held under administrative detention for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他被行政拘留了两周。
senses.why: Officials can act directly on citizens, so the adjective separates their decisions from judicial ones.
senses.whyCN: 官员能直接对公民采取措施，这个形容词便把他们的决定与司法决定区分开。

intro.en: Administrative is the adjective of administer, and the family goes back to a Latin word for a servant.
intro.cn: administrative 是 administer 的形容词，这一族词都能追到拉丁语里表示「仆人」的词。

items.en: Minister meant a servant who attends to another person.
items.cn: minister 意为在旁侍候他人的仆人。

items.en: Ministrare meant to serve or to supply what is needed.
items.cn: ministrare 意为服务，或提供所需之物。

items.en: The compound added direction and grew the sense of managing affairs.
items.cn: 复合词加上方向，并发展出「管理事务」的意思。

items.en: The adjective administrativus is recorded in medieval Latin, meaning relating to management; some sources call its formation uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 administrativus 见于中世纪拉丁语，义为「与管理有关的」；其构成方式有来源不确定之处。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective for the conduct of public and private affairs.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，用于公共与私人事务的处理。

items.en: Politics fixed the sense of government business, and offices fixed the sense of paperwork.
items.cn: 政治固定了「政务」义，办公室固定了「文书事务」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the administer family; the near-meaning group covers management, government and officialdom.
note.cn: 形近组是 administer 这一族词；近义组覆盖管理、政务与官员体系。

entries.definition: To manage affairs or give a treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理；施行；给药」，是本族的动词基础。

entries.definition: The activity of managing or the body that manages.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政部门」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A person who manages an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: In a way that relates to management or official procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在行政上」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to the work of managing people or a business.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「管理的、经理层的」，偏重对人的管理。

entries.definition: Relating to the part of an organization that puts decisions into effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「执行的、决策层的」，偏重执行权。

entries.definition: Relating to rigid official procedure, often with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「官僚的、繁文缛节的」，常带贬义。

entries.definition: Approved by or belonging to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「官方的、正式的」，强调来自权威。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the same family from a servant's duty to a signed form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着同一族词，从仆人的职责走到一份签好的表格。

normal.en: Administrative is administer plus -ive, so it means having the nature of managing.
normal.cn: administrative 是 administer 加 -ive，所以它的意思是「具有管理性质的」。

normal.en: The root minister means servant, which is why administrative work is still service work.
normal.cn: 词根 minister 意为仆人，所以行政工作至今仍是服务工作。

normal.en: Administrative staff are the people who keep the rules and records.
normal.cn: administrative staff 指维护规章与记录的那批人。

normal.en: Administrative costs are the money spent on running an office rather than on the product.
normal.cn: administrative costs 指花在办公运转上、而非产品本身的费用。

normal.en: Administrative detention is a decision by officials, not by a court.
normal.cn: administrative detention 是官员作出的决定，而不是法院的判决。

abstract.en: A desk where every paper receives a red stamp before it moves on.
abstract.cn: 一张办公桌，每份文件在传走之前都被盖上一枚红章。

abstract.en: A chain of signatures climbing from one office to the next.
abstract.cn: 一串签名从一间办公室爬到下一间办公室。

abstract.en: A wall of folders that quietly decides who waits and who proceeds.
abstract.cn: 一堵文件夹的墙，悄悄决定谁要等待、谁可放行。

examples.en: The administrative staff handled all the paperwork.
examples.cn: 行政人员处理了所有文书工作。

examples.en: She was given an administrative post in the ministry.
examples.cn: 她在部里获得了一个行政职位。

examples.en: The reform cut administrative costs by a third.
examples.cn: 这项改革把行政成本削减了三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德迷你斯特拉提夫」——阿德迷你地在一张小桌后处理公文

root: 源自拉丁语 administrativus，出自 administrare「服务、管理」，后者又出自 minister「仆人」；因此这个词从「为事务提供服务」出发，发展出「管理的」「政务的」「文书事务的」以及「由行政机关作出的」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: running an organization, governing a region, handling paperwork, and deciding as an official body.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：管理组织、治理地区、处理文书事务、以行政机关身份作出决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped document carries a decision from one desk to a whole institution.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份盖了章的文件，把决定从一张桌子带到整个机构。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: daily affairs are managed and kept moving.
branches.cn: 办公线：日常事务被管理并持续运转。

branches.en: THE STATE: a government administers a whole territory.
branches.cn: 国家线：政府管辖整片土地。

branches.en: THE PAPER: forms and records mark the routine layer of work.
branches.cn: 文书线：表格与记录标出日常工作的那一层。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL ORDER: an authority acts without waiting for a court.
branches.cn: 行政命令线：当局不必等法院即可行动。

branches.en: THE SERVICE: both management and paperwork answer the needs of an institution.
branches.cn: 服务线：管理与文书都在回应机构的需要。

intro.en: Administrative joins a Latin prefix and a Latin verb, then adds an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: administrative 由一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁动词构成，再加上英语形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin minister, ministrare, administrare and administrativus are recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minister、ministrare、administrare 与 administrativus 均有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It adds direction to the verb.
The servant is the heart of the family.
items.exampleCN: 仆人这个词是整个词族的核心。

items.example: It names the act of serving.
It is the direct source of administer.
items.exampleCN: 它是 administer 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the model for the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语这个形容词的范本。

由 administrate 加 -tion 构成，义为「管理、行政部门」
义为「管理、实施」，是 administrators 的动词基础

definition_zh: 钦佩；敬佩；欣赏；称赞；（旧用法）惊叹
definition_en: to respect someone highly, to look at something with pleasure, or to praise it openly
core_image: 一个人停在画前，眼睛发亮，忍不住轻轻点头
scene: 海边的观景台上，游客们停下了脚步，久久望向天边。They stood in silence to admire the colours of the sunset.
sceneCN: 这里 admire 是「欣赏、观赏」（第 2 个义项：带着愉悦观看）；句意为他们静静站着欣赏落日的色彩。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「钦佩、赞赏」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「仰慕者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「赞赏的」
由本词词干加 -able 构成，义为「令人钦佩的」

senses.title: To respect and approve of someone
senses.definition: to have a high opinion of someone because of their qualities or achievements
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的品质或成就而对其怀有很高的评价
senses.example: I admire her for speaking up when everyone else stayed silent.
senses.exampleCN: 我钦佩她在众人沉默时敢于发声。
senses.why: The Latin verb admirari began as 'to wonder at', and wonder at a person's quality turns into respect.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 admirari 本义是「对……感到惊奇」，对他人的惊奇便转为敬佩。

senses.title: To look at something with pleasure
senses.definition: to look at something beautiful or impressive with enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 带着愉悦观看美丽或令人赞叹的事物
senses.example: We stood on the bridge to admire the sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 我们站在桥上欣赏落日。
senses.why: The same wondering gaze is turned toward an object rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 同一种惊叹的目光从人转向了物。

senses.title: To praise openly
senses.definition: to express approval or praise for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物表达赞许或称赞
senses.example: The coach admired the young player's courage.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞了这名年轻球员的勇气。
senses.why: Admiration spoken aloud becomes praise, the outward form of an inner high opinion.
senses.whyCN: 把敬佩说出口就成了称赞，是内心高评价的外在形式。

senses.title: To wonder at, in older literary use
senses.definition: in older literary English, to regard something with wonder or astonishment
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文学英语中，怀着惊奇或惊叹看待某事物
senses.example: The travellers admired the strange lights above the moor.
senses.exampleCN: 旅人们惊叹于荒原上空奇异的光。
senses.why: This sense keeps the oldest meaning of mirari, 'to wonder', before respect and pleasure split off.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了 mirari「惊奇」的最古老含义，在敬佩与愉悦分化之前。

intro.en: Admire comes from a Latin verb of wonder and reaches English through Old French.
intro.cn: admire 出自一个表示「惊奇」的拉丁动词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Mirari meant to wonder or be astonished at something.
items.cn: mirari 意为对某事物感到惊奇或惊愕。

items.en: The prefix ad- added direction, giving 'to wonder at'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 加上方向，构成「对……感到惊奇」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb onward with the sense of regarding with wonder.
items.cn: 古法语承接了这个动词，保留「怀着惊奇看待」的意思。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Respect, visual pleasure and open praise became the three everyday senses.
items.cn: 敬佩、视觉愉悦与公开称赞成为三个日常义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the wonder root; the near-meaning group gathers ways of valuing people and things.
note.cn: 形近组共享「惊奇」词根；近义组收表示看重人或物的各种说法。

entries.definition: The feeling of respecting and approving of someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「钦佩、赞赏」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A person who admires someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「仰慕者」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Deserving respect and approval.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人钦佩的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A glass surface that shows a reflection; from the same wonder root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「镜子」，出自同一「凝视、惊奇」词根。

entries.definition: To treat someone with esteem; cooler and less emotional than admire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊敬」，比 admire 更冷静、更少情感色彩。

entries.definition: To value someone highly, especially in a formal or considered way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊重、看重」，语气正式。

entries.definition: To feel deep respect for someone or something sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇敬」，带有对神圣事物的敬意。

entries.definition: To recognize the value of something, often with enjoyment.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣赏、赏识」，强调认识到价值。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real wonder root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的「惊奇」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Admire is ad- plus mirari, 'to wonder at', so admiration begins as astonishment.
normal.cn: admire 是 ad- 加 mirari「对……惊奇」，所以钦佩最初源于惊叹。

normal.en: The same root gives mirror, because a mirror is something you gaze at.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 mirror，因为镜子正是让人凝视之物。

normal.en: Admire somebody for something is the standard pattern for respect.
normal.cn: admire somebody for something 是表达敬佩的标准搭配。

normal.en: You admire a view when your eyes enjoy it.
normal.cn: 当眼睛享受一处景色时，你用 admire a view。

normal.en: Admiration is the noun and admirable is the adjective of the same family.
normal.cn: admiration 是名词，admirable 是同一词族的形容词。

abstract.en: A visitor stopping still in front of a painting, eyes bright.
abstract.cn: 一位访客在一幅画前停住脚步，眼睛发亮。

abstract.en: Silent applause that never needs to become sound.
abstract.cn: 无声的掌声，始终不必真的响起来。

abstract.en: A mirror that reflects not the face but the wonder in the eyes.
abstract.cn: 一面镜子，照出的不是面容，而是眼中的惊奇。

examples.en: I admire your patience with the children.
examples.cn: 我钦佩你对孩子们的耐心。

examples.en: They stopped to admire the old bridge.
examples.cn: 他们停下来欣赏那座古桥。

examples.en: We admire her for never giving up.
examples.cn: 我们敬佩她从不放弃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿麦尔」——阿麦尔站在画前，越看越佩服

root: 源自拉丁语 admirari「对……感到惊奇」，由 ad-「向」加 mirari「惊奇」构成；mirari 又生出 mirror「镜子」等词。核心义由「惊叹」发展为「敬佩」「欣赏」「称赞」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: respecting a person, enjoying a sight, praising openly, and the older sense of wondering.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：敬佩某人、欣赏景物、公开称赞，以及较早的「惊叹」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stops before something impressive and cannot look away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人停在令人赞叹的事物前，目光久久不移。

branches.en: THE PERSON: wonder at someone's quality settles into respect.
branches.cn: 人线：对他人才质的惊叹沉淀为敬佩。

branches.en: THE SCENE: the same gaze turns to beauty and takes pleasure in it.
branches.cn: 景物线：同一目光转向美，并从中获得愉悦。

branches.en: THE VOICE: inner respect comes out as spoken praise.
branches.cn: 声音线：内心的敬佩化为说出口的称赞。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: wonder itself, before respect and pleasure separated.
branches.cn: 古义线：在敬佩与愉悦分化之前的惊奇本身。

branches.en: THE GAZE: whether at a person or a view, the eyes lead the feeling.
branches.cn: 凝视线：无论对人还是对景，都是眼睛先引出情感。

intro.en: Admire is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb of wondering, with English suffixes building the family.
intro.cn: admire 由一个拉丁前缀加一个表示「惊奇」的拉丁动词构成，英语后缀再扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari, admirari and the noun admiratio are recorded, so only the deeper origin of mirari is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mirari、admirari 与名词 admiratio 均有记录，只有 mirari 更早的来源不确定。

items.example: It directs the wondering toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把惊奇的目光引向某个对象。

items.example: It is the root of the whole family.
It is the direct source of admire.
items.exampleCN: 它是 admire 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the model for admiration.

definition_zh: 承认；供认；准许进入；接纳；容许
definition_en: to agree that something is true, to allow someone to enter, to accept someone into a group, or to leave room for something
core_image: 一扇门被推开，承认错误的人低着头走进房间
scene: 面试结束后，年轻人犹豫了很久，终于把隐瞒的错误说了出来。He finally admitted that he had lied on the form.
sceneCN: 这里 admit 是「承认」（第 1 个义项：承认某事为真）；句意为他终于承认自己在表格上撒了谎。

pos.zh: 承认；供认；准许进入；接纳；容许

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -sion 构成，义为「承认；准入；入场费」
由本词词干加 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的」
由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「进入权」
由过去分词 admitted 加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然」

senses.title: To confess something true
senses.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true or that one has done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 常指不情愿地承认某事为真或自己做了错事
senses.example: He finally admitted that he had lied on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 他终于承认自己在表格上撒了谎。
senses.why: The Latin ad- adds direction to mittere, 'to send', so admitting is sending a hidden fact out into the open.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 ad- 给 mittere「送」加上方向，所以承认就是把隐藏的事实送到明处。

senses.title: To allow someone to enter
senses.definition: to allow a person or thing to enter a place
senses.definitionCN: 允许人或物进入某处
senses.example: The guard admitted us through the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫让我们从侧门进去。
senses.why: From 'send toward', the verb came to mean letting someone come in.
senses.whyCN: 从「朝这边送」出发，这个词发展出「让人进来」的意思。

senses.title: To accept into an institution
senses.definition: to accept someone into a school, hospital, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 接收某人进入学校、医院或组织
senses.example: She was admitted to the university last autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年秋天被这所大学录取。
senses.why: An institution opens its gate and sends the newcomer inward, so entry becomes membership.
senses.whyCN: 机构打开大门，把新人送进内部，于是「进入」变成了「成为成员」。

senses.title: To accept as valid
senses.definition: to accept evidence, a claim, or a proposal as valid
senses.definitionCN: 承认证据、主张或提议有效
senses.example: The court refused to admit the recording as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拒绝把这段录音作为证据采纳。
senses.why: A court lets a piece of proof enter the case, using the same gate image.
senses.whyCN: 法庭让一份证据「进入」案件，用的仍是同一道门的意象。

senses.title: To allow room for
senses.definition: to allow something to be possible, used in the pattern admit of
senses.definitionCN: 容许某事成为可能，用于 admit of 这一结构
senses.example: The plan admits of no delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划不容许有任何延误。
senses.why: If a situation admits something, it opens a space for it rather than shutting it out.
senses.whyCN: 如果一种情况 admits 某事，就是给它留出空间，而不是把它关在外面。

intro.en: Admit comes from a Latin verb meaning to send toward, and its family split into admitting facts and admitting people.
intro.cn: admit 出自一个意为「朝……送」的拉丁动词，这一族后来分成承认事实与放人进入两条线。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放行。

items.en: Ad- plus mittere gave 'to send toward, let in, allow'.
items.cn: ad- 加 mittere 构成「朝……送、放进来、允许」。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English with both the entry and the acceptance senses.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，「进入」与「接受」两个义项当时已并存。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Law added the sense of accepting evidence, while everyday speech kept confession and entry.
items.cn: 法律添上「采纳证据」义，日常口语则保留「承认」与「进入」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the admit family; the near-meaning group gathers confessions, permissions and acknowledgements.
note.cn: 形近组是 admit 这一族词；近义组收承认、允许与确认三类说法。

entries.definition: The act of admitting or the price of entry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认、准入、入场费」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Allowed to be used, especially as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的」，多用于证据。

entries.definition: The right or permission to enter a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Used to concede that a point is true.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认」，由过去分词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To admit wrongdoing, often formally or emotionally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坦白、供认」，语气更强，多指承认过错。

entries.definition: To accept that something is true or exists, often more neutral than admit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、确认」，比 admit 更中性。

entries.definition: To admit a point reluctantly, often in an argument.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「勉强承认」，多用于争论中让步。

entries.definition: To allow something to happen or someone to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「允许、准许」，对应「准入」义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the 'send toward' root from a spoken confession to an open gate.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着「朝……送」的词根，从说出口的坦白走到打开的门。

normal.en: Mittere means to send, so admit is to send a fact or a person forward.
normal.cn: mittere 意为「送」，所以 admit 就是把事实或人往前送。

normal.en: Admission is the noun, and an admission ticket still uses the same gate image.
normal.cn: admission 是名词，而入场券仍沿用同一道门的意象。

normal.en: Admit defeat is to send your resistance out of the room.
normal.cn: admit defeat 就是把自己的抵抗送出房间，也就是认输。

normal.en: A hospital admits a patient when it lets that person in for care.
normal.cn: 医院让病人进去接受治疗，就是 admit a patient。

normal.en: Admit of means leaving room for, not closing the door.
normal.cn: admit of 意为留有余地，而不是把门关上。

abstract.en: A narrow gate with a guard who finally steps aside.
abstract.cn: 一道窄门，守卫终于让到一旁。

abstract.en: A hidden note pushed across the table into the light.
abstract.cn: 一张藏起来的纸条被推到桌面，暴露在光下。

abstract.en: Two doors, one for truth and one for people, opening together.
abstract.cn: 两扇门，一扇给真相，一扇给人，同时打开。

examples.en: She admitted that she had made a mistake.
examples.cn: 她承认自己犯了错。

examples.en: The museum admits visitors until five o'clock.
examples.cn: 博物馆开放到五点。

examples.en: He was admitted to the hospital for tests.
examples.cn: 他入院接受检查。

root: 源自拉丁语 admittere「朝……送、放进来」，由 ad-「向」加 mittere「送」构成；古法语 admettere 将其带入英语。核心意象是「把事实或人送进门的另一侧」，由此分出「承认」「准入」「接纳」「采纳」「容许」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: confessing a fact, letting a person in, accepting a member, accepting evidence, and leaving room for something.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：承认事实、放人进入、接收成员、采纳证据、容许某事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate opens and something hidden is sent into the open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门打开，原本隐藏的东西被送进明处。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: a hidden fact is sent out into the open.
branches.cn: 真相线：隐藏的事实被送到明处。

branches.en: THE GATE: a person is allowed through.
branches.cn: 门线：一个人获准通过。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: entry becomes membership.
branches.cn: 机构线：进入变成成员身份。

branches.en: THE COURT: proof is allowed into the case.
branches.cn: 法庭线：证据获准进入案件。

branches.en: THE OPEN SPACE: a possibility is given room rather than refused.
branches.cn: 余地在：一种可能性被留出空间，而非被拒绝。

intro.en: Admit joins a Latin prefix and a Latin verb of sending; English builds the family with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: admit 由一个拉丁前缀和一个表示「送」的拉丁动词构成，英语再用普通后缀扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere, admittere and admissio are recorded, so only the deeper origin of mittere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere、admittere 与 admissio 均有记录，只有 mittere 更早的来源不确定。

items.example: It turns sending into sending toward.

items.exampleCN: 它是 admit 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the model for admission.

definition_zh: 诚然；无可否认地；据本人承认
definition_en: used to admit that something is true before adding a contrasting point, or in a way acknowledged by everyone
core_image: 说话者先举起一只手，承认对方有理，再继续自己的话
scene: 讨论越拖越久，双方都不肯先松口，会议室里安静下来。Admittedly, the plan is expensive, but it may save money later.
sceneCN: 这里 admittedly 是「诚然、无可否认」（第 1 个义项：先承认某点为真）；句意为诚然这个计划很贵，但以后可能省钱。

pos.zh: 诚然；无可否认地；据本人承认

senses.title: Conceding a point before a contrast
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to admit that a point is true before making a contrasting statement
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，先承认某一点为真，再提出对比性的说法
senses.example: Admittedly, the plan is expensive, but it may save money later.
senses.exampleCN: 诚然，这个计划很贵，但以后可能省钱。
senses.why: The adverb marks an admission already made, turning the confession into a stepping stone for argument.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记一个已经作出的承认，把坦白变成论证的垫脚石。

senses.title: As acknowledged by everyone
senses.definition: in a way that is accepted as true by most people
senses.definitionCN: 以多数人都承认为真的方式
senses.example: The view is admittedly beautiful, even in bad weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这景色确实美，即使天气不好也一样。
senses.why: Admitted here means accepted, so the adverb simply says the fact is beyond dispute.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 admitted 意为「被接受的」，副词只是说明该事实无可争议。

senses.title: By one's own admission
senses.definition: by the speaker's or the subject's own confession
senses.definitionCN: 根据说话者或当事人自己的承认
senses.example: He is admittedly careless with details.
senses.exampleCN: 他自己也承认在细节上粗心。
senses.why: The word can point back to the person who has already confessed the weakness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以回指那个已经承认自身缺点的人。

intro.en: Admittedly is simply admitted plus -ly, and admitted is the past participle of admit.
intro.cn: admittedly 就是 admitted 加 -ly，而 admitted 是 admit 的过去分词。

items.en: Mittere meant to send, the root behind admit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送」，是 admit 背后的词根。

items.en: Admittere meant to send toward or let in.
items.cn: admittere 意为「朝……送、放进来」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fifteenth century with the sense of accepting a fact.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪进入英语，带有「接受事实」的意思。

items.en: The past participle came to mean 'acknowledged', as in an admitted fact.
items.cn: 过去分词发展出「被承认的」之意，如 an admitted fact。

items.en: Adding -ly turned the participle into an adverb of concession.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 后，这个分词变成表示让步的副词。

items.en: The adverb settled at the start of a sentence to soften a concession.
items.cn: 这个副词固定在句首，用来缓和让步的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group is the admit family; the near-meaning group gathers other concessive and affirmative adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 admit 这一族词；近义组收其他表示让步或肯定的副词。

entries.definition: To acknowledge a fact or allow entry.

entries.definition: The act of admitting or the right to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认；准入」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Allowed to be accepted, especially as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Used to agree strongly or state something as sure.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「当然、确实」，表示强烈同意。

entries.definition: Used to accept a point before arguing, close to admittedly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或连接词，义为「诚然、就算如此」，用法与 admittedly 接近。

entries.definition: Used to confirm or emphasize that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「确实、的确」，用来确认或强调。

entries.definition: By one's own admission, in a formal or literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「据承认」，语气正式或偏文学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the adverb out of the participle and its concessive use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从这个分词及其让步用法出发，拼出这个副词。

normal.en: Admitted means acknowledged, so admittedly means in an acknowledged way.
normal.cn: admitted 意为「被承认的」，所以 admittedly 意为「以被承认的方式」。

normal.en: The -ly ending turns the participle into a sentence adverb.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ly 把这个分词变成句子副词。

normal.en: It usually sits first in the clause: admittedly, the cost is high.
normal.cn: 它通常位于句首：诚然，成本很高。

normal.en: It often pairs with but, because it prepares a contrast.
normal.cn: 它常与 but 呼应，因为它是在为对比作铺垫。

normal.en: The same family gives admission and admissible.

abstract.en: A hand raised briefly before the argument continues.
abstract.cn: 一只短暂举起的手，然后争论继续。

abstract.en: One stone laid down so the path can go on.
abstract.cn: 先放下一块石头，路才能继续往前。

abstract.en: A door held open for the other side's point.
abstract.cn: 为一方的观点扶住门，让它先通过。

examples.en: Admittedly, the first attempt failed.
examples.cn: 无可否认，第一次尝试失败了。

examples.en: The task is admittedly harder than we expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务确实比我们预想的更难。

examples.en: He is admittedly not the fastest runner.
examples.cn: 他自己也承认不是跑得最快的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker raises one hand to concede before continuing.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话者先举起一只手表示承认，然后继续说下去。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: a point is granted so the main claim can stand.
branches.cn: 论证线：先让出一个点，主论点才站得住。

branches.en: THE CROWD: what everyone accepts needs no dispute.
branches.cn: 众人线：人人都接受的事无需争辩。

branches.en: THE SELF: the subject's own confession supplies the proof.

branches.en: THE COMMON GROUND: concession and public agreement both clear the way.
branches.cn: 共识线：让步与公认都在为后续铺路。

branches.en: THE ADMISSION: whether tactical or personal, something is openly granted.
branches.cn: 承认线：无论出于策略还是个人，总有某点被公开让出。

senses.title: The period between childhood and adulthood
senses.definition: the stage of life between being a child and being an adult
senses.definitionCN: 处于儿童与成人之间的生命阶段
senses.example: Adolescence brings rapid changes in body and mood.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期带来身体与情绪上的急剧变化。
senses.why: The Latin root means to grow up, so the noun names the stretch of time when growth is fastest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「长大」，所以这个名词指成长最迅速的那段时间。

senses.title: The process of growing up
senses.definition: the ongoing process of developing from a child into an adult
senses.definitionCN: 从儿童发展为成人的持续过程
senses.example: Adolescence is not a single moment but a long process.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期不是一个瞬间，而是一个漫长的过程。
senses.why: The same noun can name the activity of growing, not only the period it fills.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也能指「成长」这项活动，而不只是它所占据的时期。

senses.title: An early stage in the development of something
senses.definition: a youthful or early stage in the growth of an industry, idea, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 行业、观念或组织发展中的年轻阶段
senses.example: The industry is still in its adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业仍处在发展初期。
senses.why: Growing up is used as a metaphor: anything young is said to pass through its own adolescence.
senses.whyCN: 「长大」被用作比喻：任何年轻的事物都被说成经历自己的青春期。

intro.en: Adolescence comes from a Latin verb for growing up, built on a root meaning to nourish.
intro.cn: adolescence 出自一个表示「长大」的拉丁动词，其词根意为「滋养」。

items.en: Alere meant to feed or nourish.
items.cn: alere 意为喂养、滋养。

items.en: The inceptive form alescere meant to begin to grow.
items.cn: 表起始的 alescere 意为「开始生长」。

items.en: Ad- plus alescere gave adolescere, to grow up toward adulthood.
items.cn: ad- 加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为朝成年长大。

items.en: The noun adolescentia named the period and the process of growing up.
items.cn: 名词 adolescentia 指成长的时期与过程。

items.en: Old French carried the noun toward English in the sense of youth.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语，义为「青春」。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十五世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the growing-up root; the near-meaning group gathers stages and companions of youth.
note.cn: 形近组共享「长大」词根；近义组收青春期的阶段与相关说法。

entries.definition: A young person in this stage, or the adjective for it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青少年；青春期的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A fully grown person; from the same verb of growing up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「成年人；成年的」，出自同一「长大」动词。

entries.definition: The state of being an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年期」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The stage just before adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期前」，由本词加前缀构成。

entries.definition: The period of being young, or young people as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春；青年」，范围比 adolescence 更宽。

entries.definition: The biological stage when a child's body becomes sexually mature.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期发育」，偏生理学，指身体成熟的过程。

entries.definition: The years of a person's age from thirteen to nineteen.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十几岁」，按年龄划分。

entries.definition: The state of being fully grown or developed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成熟」，是青春期之后的阶段。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real root of nourishing and growing, plus the stages around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「滋养、生长」的真实词根，以及它前后的阶段。

normal.en: Alere means to nourish, and adolescence is the growth fed by that root.
normal.cn: alere 意为滋养，adolescence 就是由这个词根喂养出的成长。

normal.en: Adolescere means to grow up, so the noun names the growing-up period.
normal.cn: adolescere 意为长大，所以这个名词指成长的时期。

normal.en: Adolescent is the person; adolescence is the stage.
normal.cn: adolescent 指人，adolescence 指阶段。

normal.en: Adulthood follows adolescence, and both come from the same verb.
normal.cn: 成年期接着青春期，两者出自同一个动词。

normal.en: We say an industry is in its adolescence when it is young and changing fast.
normal.cn: 当某个行业年轻且变化迅速时，我们说它处在青春期。

abstract.en: A young tree whose branches suddenly lengthen before the leaves fill in.
abstract.cn: 一棵小树，枝条突然拉长，叶子却还没长满。

abstract.en: A voice that breaks in the middle of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 一句话说到一半，嗓音忽然变调。

abstract.en: A doorway between two rooms that keeps widening.

examples.cn: 青春期形成的许多习惯会持续一生。

examples.en: She studied the psychology of adolescence.
examples.cn: 她研究青春期心理学。

examples.en: The company went through its adolescence in the early years.
examples.cn: 这家公司在早期经历了它的成长阶段。

root: 源自拉丁语 adolescentia，出自 adolescere「长大」，由 ad-「向」加 alescere「开始生长」构成，而 alescere 又出自 alere「滋养」。因此这个词的核心是「被滋养着向上生长」，既指青春期，也指事物的成长初期。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the life stage, the process of growing, and the youthful stage of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：人生阶段、成长过程，以及任何事物的年轻阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young tree shoots upward before its leaves are fully open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵小树在叶子完全展开前先向上抽条。

branches.en: THE YEARS: the stage between childhood and adulthood.
branches.cn: 年岁线：童年与成年之间的阶段。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: growing up is an activity, not a fixed date.
branches.cn: 过程线：成长是一项持续活动，而不是一个固定日期。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: an industry or idea has its own young stage.
branches.cn: 比喻线：行业或观念也有自己的年轻阶段。

branches.en: THE BODY: the period and the bodily change are felt together.
branches.cn: 身体线：时期与身体变化被一起感受到。

branches.en: THE BEGINNING: whether a person or a project, the start is fast and unsettled.
branches.cn: 开端线：无论人还是项目，起点都迅速而未定。

intro.en: Adolescence is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb of growth, and an English noun ending.

latinIntro.en: Latin alere, alescere, adolescere and adolescentia are recorded, so only the deeper origin of alere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alere、alescere、adolescere 与 adolescentia 均有记录，只有 alere 更早的来源不确定。

definition_zh: 青少年；青春期的；不成熟的
definition_en: a young person growing from a child into an adult, or something relating to that stage
core_image: 一个正在长个子的少年，鞋码每个月都在变

sceneCN: 这里 adolescent 是名词「青少年」（第 1 个义项：处于青春期的年轻人）；句意为班里每个青少年似乎都在夏天长高了。

senses.title: A young person in the growing stage
senses.definition: a person who is developing from a child into an adult
senses.definitionCN: 正从儿童发育为成人的人
senses.example: Every adolescent in the class seemed to grow taller over the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 班里每个青少年似乎都在夏天长高了。
senses.why: The Latin participle means 'one who is growing up', so the person and the process share one word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词意为「正在长大的人」，所以人与过程共用同一个词。

senses.title: Relating to adolescence
senses.definition: connected with the stage of growing from child to adult
senses.definitionCN: 与从儿童成长为成人的阶段有关
senses.example: Adolescent behaviour can be impulsive and intense.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年的行为可能冲动而激烈。
senses.why: The same participle works as an adjective describing anything that belongs to that stage.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词可作形容词，描述属于那个阶段的一切。

senses.title: Immature or still developing
senses.definition: not yet fully grown or settled, used of people, ideas, or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 尚未完全成熟或稳定，可用于人、观念或组织
senses.example: The project is still at an adolescent stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目仍处在不成熟的阶段。
senses.why: Because the root means growing up, the adjective can mark anything young and unsettled.
senses.whyCN: 由于词根意为「长大」，这个形容词可标出任何年轻而未定的事物。

intro.en: Adolescent is the present participle of a Latin verb meaning to grow up.
intro.cn: adolescent 是一个意为「长大」的拉丁动词的现在分词。

items.en: Alere meant to nourish or feed.
items.cn: alere 意为滋养、喂养。

items.en: Alescere meant to begin to grow.
items.cn: alescere 意为开始生长。

items.en: Adolescere meant to grow up toward adulthood.
items.cn: adolescere 意为朝成年长大。

items.en: The participle stem adolescent- means 'growing up', and it supplied both noun and adjective.
items.cn: 分词词干 adolescent- 意为「正在长大」，同时供出名词与形容词。

items.en: Old French carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带入英语。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十五世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the growing-up root; the near-meaning group names young people in different registers.
note.cn: 形近组共享「长大」词根；近义组用不同语体称呼年轻人。

entries.definition: The stage of growing up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A fully grown person; from the same verb.

entries.definition: The state of being fully grown.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年期」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A child just before adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青春期前的」，由本词加前缀构成。

entries.definition: A person aged from thirteen to nineteen; defined by age rather than growth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十几岁的青少年」，按年龄而非发育划分。

entries.definition: A young person or young people as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青年」，可指个人或群体。

entries.definition: A young person, especially in legal contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「少年」，多用于法律语境。

entries.definition: A person below the legal age of adulthood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未成年人」，是法律年龄概念。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the verb of growing up and the legal and everyday labels around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「长大」这个动词，以及围绕它的法律与日常称呼。

normal.en: Adolescent is the person who is adolescere, growing up, in the middle of the act.
normal.cn: adolescent 就是正在 adolescere（长大）的人，正处在动作之中。

normal.en: Adolescence is the stage, adolescent is the person or the adjective.
normal.cn: adolescence 是阶段，adolescent 是人或形容词。

normal.en: The root alere means to nourish, so the adolescent is still being fed into growth.
normal.cn: 词根 alere 意为滋养，所以青少年仍在被滋养着生长。

normal.en: Adolescent behaviour is behaviour typical of that growing stage.
normal.cn: adolescent behaviour 就是那个成长阶段典型的行为。

normal.en: Adult and adolescent come from the same verb but mark the two ends of the process.
normal.cn: adult 与 adolescent 出自同一动词，却标出这一过程的两端。

abstract.en: A pair of shoes outgrown before the season ends.
abstract.cn: 一双鞋还没穿到季末就已经变小。

abstract.en: A voice that cracks between two words.
abstract.cn: 两个词之间突然破音的嗓音。

abstract.en: A sketch that has the shape but not yet the detail.
abstract.cn: 一张只有轮廓、尚无细节的草图。

examples.en: The clinic offers advice for adolescent patients.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为青少年病人提供建议。

examples.en: He was a quiet adolescent who read constantly.
examples.cn: 他是个安静的青少年，总在读书。

examples.en: Adolescent enthusiasm can fade as quickly as it comes.
examples.cn: 青少年的热情来得快，去得也快。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the growing person, the adjective for that stage, and anything still immature.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：正在成长的年轻人、属于该阶段的形容词、以及任何尚未成熟的事物。

core.cn: 核心意象：年轻的身体长得比鞋码还快。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who is in the middle of growing up.
branches.cn: 人线：正处在成长之中的人。

branches.en: THE STAGE: whatever belongs to that period is called adolescent.
branches.cn: 阶段线：属于那个时期的一切都被称为青春期的。

branches.en: THE IMMATURE: ideas and projects can be young too.

branches.en: THE BODY: the person and the bodily stage are inseparable.

intro.cn: adolescent 是一个拉丁分词词干，英语把它同时用作名词和形容词。

definition_en: to take a child legally as one's own, or to start using and accepting a plan, method, role, or name
core_image: 一双手把一份陌生的方案捧起，放进自己的工具箱
scene: 社区开会时，居民们围坐一圈，讨论怎样让旧厂房重新有用。The council decided to adopt the plan for a riverside park.
sceneCN: 这里 adopt 是「采纳、采用」（第 2 个义项：开始采用某种计划或方法）；句意为议会决定采纳在河边建公园的计划。

pos.zh: 收养；采用；采纳；正式通过；承担

senses.title: To take a child legally as one's own
senses.definition: to take another person's child into one's family and raise it as one's own
senses.definitionCN: 把他人的孩子接入自己家庭并当作亲生子女抚养
senses.example: The couple adopted a child from the local orphanage.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇从当地孤儿院收养了一个孩子。
senses.why: The Latin optare means to choose, so adopting is choosing a child to bring into the family.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 optare 意为「选择」，收养就是选择把孩子带入家庭。

senses.title: To start using a plan or method
senses.definition: to begin to use an idea, method, or plan as one's own
senses.definitionCN: 开始把某种观念、方法或计划当作自己的来使用
senses.example: The council decided to adopt the plan for a riverside park.
senses.exampleCN: 议会决定采纳在河边建公园的计划。
senses.why: Choosing a plan and taking it into one's practice is the same movement as choosing a child into the family.
senses.whyCN: 选定一个计划并把它纳入自己的实践，与选定一个孩子进入家庭是同一个动作。

senses.title: To accept formally as a body
senses.definition: to approve and accept a proposal officially, as a committee or assembly
senses.definitionCN: 由委员会或议会正式批准并接受某项提案
senses.example: The committee voted to adopt the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会投票通过了新规则。
senses.why: A group votes to choose a text, and formal approval is the public side of adoption.
senses.whyCN: 团体通过投票选定一份文本，而正式批准是「采纳」的公开一面。

senses.title: To take on a role or attitude
senses.definition: to take on a role, attitude, or manner for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为特定目的承担某种角色、态度或举止
senses.example: He adopted a calm tone despite the anger.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管很愤怒，他还是采取了平静的语气。
senses.why: An attitude can be chosen and worn like a garment, so one adopts it as one adopts a plan.
senses.whyCN: 态度可以被选择并像衣服一样穿上，所以人 adopt 它也像 adopt 一个计划。

senses.title: To take a name or custom as one's own
senses.definition: to begin to use a name, spelling, or custom as one's own
senses.definitionCN: 开始把某个名字、拼写或风俗当作自己的来使用
senses.example: After moving abroad, she adopted a shorter surname.
senses.exampleCN: 移居国外后，她采用了一个更短的姓氏。
senses.why: A choice is made and something is taken up permanently, whether it is a name or a custom.
senses.whyCN: 作出选择并永久接受某物，无论那是一个名字还是一种风俗。

intro.en: Adopt joins a Latin prefix of direction to a Latin verb meaning to choose.
intro.cn: adopt 把一个表示方向、向……的拉丁前缀和一个意为「选择」的拉丁动词合在一起。

items.en: Optare meant to choose or desire.
items.cn: optare 意为选择、愿望。

items.en: Ad- plus optare gave 'to choose for oneself, take as one's own'.
items.cn: ad- 加 optare 构成「为自己选定、当作自己的」。

items.en: The noun named the legal act of taking a child into a family.
items.cn: 这个名词指把孩子接入家庭的合法行为。

items.en: Old French carried the verb toward English with the family sense.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，带有家庭义。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from a child to a plan, a role, a name, and a custom.
items.cn: 词义从孩子扩展到计划、角色、名字与风俗。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adopt family; the near-meaning group gathers choosing and accepting verbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 adopt 这一族词；近义组收选择与接受类的动词。

entries.definition: The act of adopting a child or a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养；采用」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Relating to adoption, as in adoptive parents.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「收养的」，如养父母。

entries.definition: Able to be adopted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可收养的；可采用的」。

entries.definition: A person who adopts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养人；采用者」。

entries.definition: To accept an idea or change eagerly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣然接受」，比 adopt 更积极热情。

entries.definition: To agree to receive or approve something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受、认可」，是最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: To take on a role, duty, or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、呈现」，对应「承担角色」义项。

entries.definition: To raise a child temporarily without legal adoption.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「寄养」，指暂时抚养，不一定取得法定收养关系，词源与 adopt 不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the Latin verb of choosing to the modern senses of taking something in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把拉丁语「选择」动词与现代「接纳入内」的各个义项连起来。

normal.en: Optare means to choose, so adopt is to choose something and take it as your own.
normal.cn: optare 意为选择，所以 adopt 就是选定某物并把它当作自己的。

normal.en: The same root gives option and optional, all about choosing.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 option 与 optional，都与选择有关。

normal.en: Adoption is the noun for taking a child or a plan into the family or the system.
normal.cn: adoption 是用作名词，指把孩子或计划接入家庭或体系。

normal.en: A committee adopts a proposal when it formally approves it.
normal.cn: 委员会正式批准提案时，就是 adopt a proposal。

normal.en: You adopt a tone the way you adopt a coat, putting it on for the occasion.
normal.cn: 人 adopt 一种语气，就像 adopt 一件外套，为某个场合穿上它。

abstract.en: A pair of hands lifting a document into a toolbox.
abstract.cn: 一双手把文件抬进工具箱。

abstract.en: An empty chair at a family table being filled.
abstract.cn: 家庭餐桌旁的一把空椅子被填满。

abstract.en: A coat chosen from a rack and worn out the door.
abstract.cn: 从衣架上挑一件外套，穿着它出门。

examples.en: They adopted a girl from the same town.
examples.cn: 他们收养了同镇的一个女孩。

examples.en: The school adopted a new method of teaching reading.
examples.cn: 学校采用了新的阅读教学法。

examples.en: She adopted a new surname after the marriage.
examples.cn: 婚后她改用了一个新姓氏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands lift a chosen document into a personal toolbox.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把选定的文件抬进自己的工具箱。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: a child is chosen and brought inside.
branches.cn: 家庭线：孩子被选定并带入内部。

branches.en: THE METHOD: a plan is chosen and put into practice.
branches.cn: 方法线：计划被选定并投入实践。

branches.en: THE ASSEMBLY: a body formally approves the choice.
branches.cn: 议会线：团体正式批准这一选择。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a role, attitude, or name is worn as one's own.
branches.cn: 表层线：角色、态度或名字被当作自己的来穿戴。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: informal use and formal approval are two sides of the same choosing.
branches.cn: 体系线：非正式使用与正式批准是同一选择的两个侧面。

definition_zh: 热爱；崇拜；爱慕；（口语）非常喜欢
definition_en: to love and worship someone deeply, or in everyday speech to like something very much
core_image: 一个人仰望神像，双手合十，眼里满是光
scene: 小女孩每天放学都要绕到巷口，只为看一眼那只灰猫。She absolutely adores the grey cat that sleeps by the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 adore 是口语「非常喜欢」（第 2 个义项：极为喜爱）；句意为她特别喜欢那只睡在门边的灰猫。

pos.zh: 热爱；崇拜；爱慕；非常喜欢

collocations.phrase: adore the ground somebody walks on
collocations.zh: 对某人崇拜得五体投地

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「爱慕；崇拜」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「爱慕者；崇拜者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「充满爱意的」

senses.title: To love and worship deeply
senses.definition: to love someone with great intensity and reverence
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的热情与敬意爱某人
senses.example: The villagers adored the old doctor who had saved them.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们深深爱戴那位救过他们的老医生。
senses.why: Latin adorare began as 'to speak to a god', so the word carries reverence inside its love.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adorare 本义是「向神说话」，所以这个词的爱里天然带着敬意。

senses.title: To like something very much, informally
senses.definition: in everyday speech, to enjoy or like something extremely
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中，极其享受或喜欢某事物
senses.example: She absolutely adores the grey cat that sleeps by the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 她特别喜欢那只睡在门边的灰猫。
senses.why: The strong emotion of worship was borrowed for ordinary pleasures, making 'love' into 'really like'.
senses.whyCN: 崇拜的强烈情感被借来形容日常乐趣，把「爱」弱化为「特别喜欢」。

senses.title: To worship a deity
senses.definition: to honour and pray to a god or sacred being
senses.definitionCN: 敬奉并向神灵或神圣存在祈祷
senses.example: The pilgrims adored the statue at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者在黎明时分向那尊雕像礼拜。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: adorare meant to address a god with prayer.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：adorare 意为以祈祷向神灵致辞。

intro.en: Adore comes from a Latin verb of praying to a god, and its emotion later spread to people and things.
intro.cn: adore 出自一个向神灵祈祷的拉丁动词，这种情感后来扩展到人和物。

items.en: Orare meant to speak, plead, or pray.
items.cn: orare 意为说话、恳求、祈祷。

items.en: Ad- plus orare gave 'to speak to, pray to, worship'.
items.cn: ad- 加 orare 构成「向……说话、向……祈祷、崇拜」。

items.en: The noun named worship and reverence.
items.cn: 这个名词指崇拜与敬意。

items.en: Old French carried the verb toward English with the sense of deep reverence.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入英语，带有深切敬意的意思。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense weakened in casual speech to 'like very much'.
items.cn: 在随意口语中，词义弱化为「非常喜欢」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adore family; the near-meaning group moves from worship to ordinary affection.
note.cn: 形近组是 adore 这一族词；近义组从崇拜一路走到日常喜爱。

entries.definition: Deep love and worship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱慕；崇拜」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A person who adores someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱慕者；崇拜者」。

entries.definition: Full of love and reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满爱意的」，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Very lovable or charming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可爱的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: To honour and pray to a god; stronger in the religious sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「崇拜、礼拜」，宗教意味更强。

entries.definition: To love and value someone or something dearly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「珍爱」，强调珍惜与呵护。

entries.definition: To admire someone excessively, almost as a god.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「把……偶像化」，带有过度崇拜意味。

entries.definition: To feel deep affection for someone; broader and less marked than adore.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「爱」，范围更广，情感色彩不如 adore 强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the prayer root and the modern weakening of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「祈祷」词根，以及这个词在现代的语义弱化。

normal.en: Orare means to pray, so adore began as praying to a god.
normal.cn: orare 意为祈祷，所以 adore 最初是向神灵祈祷。

normal.en: Adoration is the noun, and it still sounds religious.
normal.cn: adoration 是名词，至今仍带宗教色彩。

normal.en: Adorable came from the same family and now simply means charming.
normal.cn: adorable 出自同一词族，如今只表示「可爱」。

normal.en: In casual speech, adore is a stronger form of like.
normal.cn: 在口语里，adore 是比 like 更强的说法。

normal.en: To adore the ground someone walks on is the extreme image of devotion.
normal.cn: 「adore the ground somebody walks on」是崇拜至极的形象说法。

abstract.en: A figure kneeling before a lit statue at dawn.
abstract.cn: 黎明时分，一个人跪在点着灯的神像前。

abstract.en: A child hugging a cat so tightly it cannot move.
abstract.cn: 一个孩子把猫抱得紧紧的，猫都动不了。

abstract.en: A heart with a small flame that never goes out.
abstract.cn: 一颗心，上面有一簇永不熄灭的小火苗。

examples.en: The people adored their young king.
examples.cn: 人民爱戴他们年轻的国王。

examples.en: I adore walking by the river in the early morning.
examples.cn: 我非常喜欢清晨沿河散步。

examples.en: They adored the same saint for generations.
examples.cn: 他们世代崇敬同一位圣徒。

root: 源自拉丁语 adorare「向……说话、向……祈祷、崇拜」，由 ad-「向」加 orare「说话、恳求」构成；名词 adoratio 指崇拜。词义由宗教崇拜扩展到对人的深切爱慕，再在口语中弱化为「非常喜欢」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: deep loving reverence, informal strong liking, and worship of a deity.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：深切的爱与敬、口语中的强烈喜爱、对神灵的崇拜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person looks up at a statue with folded hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人双手合十，仰望神像。

branches.en: THE PERSON: reverence toward a person becomes deep love.
branches.cn: 人线：对人的敬意变成深切的爱。

branches.en: THE PLEASURE: worship's intensity is borrowed for everyday joy.
branches.cn: 愉悦线：崇拜的强度被借来形容日常乐趣。

branches.en: THE DEITY: the oldest sense keeps prayer at its centre.
branches.cn: 神灵线：最古老的义项仍以祈祷为核心。

branches.en: THE ALTAR: love and worship share one gesture of reverence.
branches.cn: 祭坛线：爱与崇拜共享同一个敬拜姿态。

branches.en: THE SCALE: the same word can be sacred or playful.
branches.cn: 尺度线：同一个词可以神圣，也可以轻松。

intro.en: Adore is a Latin prefix and a Latin verb of speaking and praying, with English suffixes around it.
intro.cn: adore 是一个拉丁前缀加一个表示说话与祈祷的拉丁动词，周围再加上英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin orare, adorare and adoratio are recorded; the deeper origin of orare is uncertain.

definition_zh: 成年人；成年的；成熟的；仅供成人使用的
definition_en: a person who is fully grown, or something relating to fully grown people
core_image: 一棵终于长到屋顶高度的树，枝叶已经完全展开
scene: 家长会上，老师们讨论怎样让孩子慢慢学会自己负责。An adult should be able to admit a mistake without blaming others.
sceneCN: 这里 adult 是名词「成年人」（第 1 个义项：完全长大的人）；句意为成年人应当能够承认错误而不责怪他人。

pos.zh: 成年的；成熟的；仅供成人使用的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -hood 构成，义为「成年期」
由本词加 -like 构成，义为「像成年人的」

senses.title: A fully grown person
senses.definition: a person who has finished growing and is legally or socially regarded as mature
senses.definitionCN: 已经完成发育、在法律或社会上被视为成熟的人
senses.example: An adult should be able to admit a mistake without blaming others.
senses.exampleCN: 成年人应当能够承认错误而不责怪他人。
senses.why: The Latin participle adultus means 'having grown up', so the person is named by the completed growth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词 adultus 意为「已经长大」，人是以「完成成长」来命名的。

senses.title: Fully grown or mature
senses.definition: having reached full size or maturity, used of people, animals, or plants
senses.definitionCN: 已达到完整大小或成熟状态，用于人、动物或植物
senses.example: The adult bird has darker feathers than the young one.
senses.exampleCN: 成年鸟的羽毛比幼鸟更深。
senses.why: The same participle works as an adjective for anything that has finished growing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词可作形容词，形容任何已经完成生长的事物。

senses.title: Intended for grown people
senses.definition: designed or suitable only for grown people, often because of mature content
senses.definitionCN: 仅为成年人设计或适合，常因内容成熟
senses.example: The film was given an adult rating.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影被评为成人级。
senses.why: Because adults are the fully grown group, anything restricted to them is simply labelled adult.
senses.whyCN: 成年人就是完全长成的那群人，凡只限他们使用的就被标为 adult。

senses.title: Behaving in a mature way
senses.definition: in informal use, showing the responsibility expected of a grown person
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中，表现出成年人应有的责任感
senses.example: It was very adult of her to apologize first.
senses.exampleCN: 她先道歉，显得非常成熟。
senses.why: The noun became a standard of behaviour, so doing it well is called being adult.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词变成了一种行为标准，所以做得好像大人就被称为 adult。

intro.en: Adult is the Latin participle of the same verb that gave adolescence and adolescent.
intro.cn: adult 与 adolescence、adolescent 出自同一个拉丁动词，是它的过去分词。

items.en: Alere meant to nourish and feed.
items.cn: alere 意为滋养、喂养。

items.en: Adolescere meant to grow up.
items.cn: adolescere 意为长大。

items.en: The past participle adultus meant 'having grown up, fully grown'.
items.cn: 过去分词 adultus 意为「已经长大、完全长成」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the seventeenth century; earlier uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个词；更早的用法不确定。

items.en: The noun, the adjective, and the informal standard of mature behaviour all developed from one participle.
items.cn: 名词、形容词与口语中的「成熟」标准，都从同一个分词发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the growing-up root; the near-meaning group covers maturity and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组共享「长大」词根；近义组覆盖成熟及其反面。

entries.definition: The stage between childhood and adulthood.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A young person still growing up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青少年；青春期的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The state of being an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年期」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Resembling an adult.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「像成年人的」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: An adult, used in a warmer or more childlike tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「大人」，语气更亲切或带孩子气。

entries.definition: Fully developed, especially in behaviour or judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「成熟的」，强调行为或判断的成熟。

entries.definition: Having reached full physical size.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完全长成的」，强调身体尺寸。

entries.definition: Behaving in a way that is immature for one's age.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「孩子气的」，是 adult 的反面对照。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the past participle 'grown up' to the noun, the adjective, and the behaviour standard.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把过去分词「已经长大」连接到名词、形容词与行为标准。

normal.en: Adultus is a past participle, so an adult is someone whose growing is done.
normal.cn: adultus 是过去分词，所以成年人就是「成长已经完成」的人。

normal.en: Adolescent is still growing; adult has finished growing.
normal.cn: adolescent 仍在生长，adult 已经长成。

normal.en: Adulthood is the noun for the whole stage.
normal.cn: adulthood 是表示整个成年阶段的名称。

normal.en: Adult education is education designed for grown people.
normal.cn: adult education 是为成年人设计的教育。

normal.en: To act adult is to act with the responsibility expected of a grown person.
normal.cn: act adult 就是以成年人应有的责任感行事。

abstract.en: A tree that finally reaches the height of the roof.
abstract.cn: 一棵树终于长到屋顶的高度。

abstract.en: A door that no longer needs someone to hold it open.
abstract.cn: 一扇不再需要别人扶着的门。

abstract.en: A coat that fits exactly, with no room left to grow.
abstract.cn: 一件正合身、再没有生长余地的外套。

examples.en: Two adults and three children were on the bus.
examples.cn: 巴士上有两名成年人和三个孩子。

examples.en: The adult stage of the insect lasts only a few days.
examples.cn: 这种昆虫的成虫阶段只持续几天。

examples.en: She handled the argument in a very adult way.
examples.cn: 她以非常成熟的方式处理了这场争执。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿道特」——阿道特已经长到门口那么高，是个大人了

root: 源自拉丁语 adultus，是 adolescere「长大」的过去分词，意为「已经长成的」；adolescere 又由 ad- 加 alescere「开始生长」构成，追溯至 alere「滋养」。因此 adult 的核心是「成长已经完成」，并由此发展出「成年人」「成年的」「成熟的」「仅供成人使用的」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the grown person, the grown state, content restricted to grown people, and mature behaviour.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：成年的人、成年的状态、仅供成人使用的内容、成熟的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree reaches the roof and stops stretching.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵树长到屋顶，便不再继续抽高。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one whose growing is complete.
branches.cn: 人线：成长已经完成的人。

branches.en: THE STATE: anything fully developed can be called adult.
branches.cn: 状态线：任何完全发育的事物都可称为成年的。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: some content is reserved for grown people.
branches.cn: 边界线：某些内容只为成年人保留。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: behaving responsibly is called being adult.
branches.cn: 标准线：负责任地行事被称为具有成人风范。

branches.en: THE BODY: the person and the fully grown state belong together.
branches.cn: 身体线：人与完全长成的状态彼此对应。

intro.en: Adult is a Latin past participle used directly in English, with suffixes building the family.
intro.cn: adult 是一个直接进入英语的拉丁过去分词，英语后缀再扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin alere, adolescere and adultus are recorded; the participle adultus is certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alere、adolescere 与 adultus 均有记录，分词 adultus 是确定的。

items.example: It marks the process before adulthood.
items.exampleCN: 它标出成年之前的过程。

由本词加 -like 构成，义为「像成年人的」

definition_zh: 前进；推进；促进；提前；预付；进展；预先的
definition_en: to move forward, make progress, help something develop, pay money before it is due, or put an idea forward
core_image: 队伍举着旗子跨过一道线，把身后的路甩开
scene: 洪水退去后，救援队沿着泥泞的道路一步步向村里推进。The rescue team began to advance along the muddy road.
sceneCN: 这里 advance 是「前进」（第 1 个义项：向前移动）；句意为救援队开始沿泥泞的道路前进。

pos.zh: 前进；推进；促进；提前；预付；提出

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「推进；进步」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「先进的；高级的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「前进的」

senses.title: To move forward
senses.definition: to move forward in space, especially toward a place or an enemy
senses.definitionCN: 在空间中向前移动，尤指朝某地或敌人推进
senses.example: The rescue team began to advance along the muddy road.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队开始沿泥泞的道路前进。
senses.why: The Old French source meant 'to move forward', built on a Latin phrase meaning 'before'.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为「向前移动」，其基础是拉丁语中表示「在前面」的短语。

senses.title: To make progress
senses.definition: to improve or move to a higher stage in knowledge, skill, or a process
senses.definitionCN: 在知识、技能或进程中改善或进入更高阶段
senses.example: Medicine has advanced greatly in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 医学在上个世纪取得了巨大进展。
senses.why: Forward motion in space becomes forward motion in time and quality.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的向前移动，转为时间与质量上的向前推进。

senses.title: To help something develop
senses.definition: to help a cause, plan, or interest move forward
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某项事业、计划或利益向前发展
senses.example: The grant advanced the study of clean energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助推动了清洁能源研究。
senses.why: To advance a cause is to push it forward as one pushes a cart.
senses.whyCN: advance 一项事业，就像推车一样把它往前推。

senses.title: To pay money before it is due
senses.definition: to pay or lend money before the agreed time
senses.definitionCN: 在约定时间之前支付或借出钱款
senses.example: The publisher advanced her part of the royalties.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社向她预付了一部分版税。
senses.why: Money is sent ahead of its due date, so it moves forward in time.
senses.whyCN: 钱在到期日之前被送出，所以在时间上「向前」了。

senses.title: To put an idea forward
senses.definition: to suggest or present an idea, theory, or proposal for consideration
senses.definitionCN: 提出某种观点、理论或提议供考虑
senses.example: She advanced a bold theory about the missing ship.
senses.exampleCN: 她提出一个关于失踪船只的大胆理论。
senses.why: An idea is brought forward into view, as a object is pushed to the front.
senses.whyCN: 观点被带到前面进入视野，就像物体被推到前排。

senses.title: Forward movement or progress
senses.definition: the noun for forward movement or a step in progress
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指向前的移动或进展中的一步
senses.example: Recent advances in medicine have saved many lives.
senses.exampleCN: 医学最近的进展挽救了许多生命。
senses.why: The verb's movement is turned into a countable thing: each step forward is an advance.
senses.whyCN: 动词的移动被转化为可数之物：每向前一步就是一个进展。

senses.title: Beforehand, in the phrase in advance
senses.definition: in the phrase in advance, before something happens or is due
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in advance，表示在某事发生或到期之前
senses.example: Book your tickets in advance to get a lower price.
senses.exampleCN: 提前订票可以拿到更低的价格。
senses.why: The noun keeps the idea of being ahead, so in advance means positioned before the event.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「在前面」的意思，所以 in advance 表示位于事件之前。

intro.en: Advance comes from Old French and rests on a Latin phrase meaning 'from before'.
intro.cn: advance 来自古法语，其底层是一个意为「从前面」的拉丁短语。

items.en: Abante meant 'from before, in front of'.
items.cn: abante 意为「从前面、在……之前」。

items.en: Avancier meant to move forward or promote.
items.cn: avancier 意为向前移动或推进。

items.en: The related noun avantage named a position in front, hence an advantage.
items.cn: 相关名词 avantage 指处于前方的位置，也就是优势。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word spread from physical movement to progress, promotion, money paid early, and ideas put forward.
items.cn: 这个词从身体移动扩展到进步、促进、提前付款与提出观点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'before' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of moving and improving.
note.cn: 形近组共享「在前」词根；近义组收移动与改进类动词。

entries.definition: The act of moving forward or improving.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推进；进步」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Highly developed or at a late stage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「先进的；高级的」，由过去分词转成。

entries.definition: Moving forward or progressing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「前进的」，由现在分词转成。

entries.definition: A position in front, hence a benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优势」，与 advance 出自同一「在前」词源。

entries.definition: To move forward or improve over time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「进展」，强调随时间改善。

entries.definition: To continue or move on to the next step.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继续进行」，强调接着往下走。

entries.definition: To help something grow or succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「促进」，对应「推动发展」义项。

entries.definition: Toward the front; to send onward.
entries.definitionCN: 副词、形容词或动词，义为「向前；转交」，方向义最直接。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow one word from a marching column to money paid early and an idea brought forward.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着同一个词，从行军队伍走到提前付款，再到被带到前面的观点。

normal.en: Abante means before, so advance is to put something in front.
normal.cn: abante 意为在前面，所以 advance 就是把某物放到前面。

normal.en: A march advances; a student advances to a higher class.
normal.cn: 队伍前进用 advance，学生升入更高年级也用 advance。

normal.en: Advance payment is money sent ahead of the due date.
normal.cn: advance payment 是在到期日之前送出的钱。

normal.en: In advance means positioned before the event.
normal.cn: in advance 意为处在事件之前。

normal.en: The same root gives advantage, a position in front.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 advantage，即处于前方的位置。

abstract.en: A column crossing a line drawn in the mud.
abstract.cn: 一支队伍跨过泥地里画出的一道线。

abstract.en: A hand pushing a paper to the front of the desk.
abstract.cn: 一只手把文件推到桌子最前面。

abstract.en: A clock whose hands move before the agreed hour.
abstract.cn: 一只在约定时刻之前就转动的钟。

examples.en: The army advanced under cover of darkness.
examples.cn: 军队在夜色掩护下前进。

examples.en: Technology advances faster than the rules can follow.
examples.cn: 技术发展得比规则跟得更快。

examples.en: You must pay a deposit in advance.
examples.cn: 你必须提前支付押金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿万斯」——阿万把旗子往前一插，队伍就前进

root: 来自古法语 avancier「向前移动、推进」，底层是拉丁语 abante「从前面、在……之前」（ab-「从」加 ante「前」）。核心是「处于或推向前面」，由此发展出「前进」「进展」「促进」「预付」「提出」以及名词「进展」「预付款」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses: moving forward, progressing, promoting, paying early, proposing, the noun for progress, and the phrase in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项：向前移动、取得进展、促进、提前付款、提出观点、名词「进展」，以及短语 in advance。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column crosses a line and leaves the road behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：队伍跨过一道线，把身后的路甩开。

branches.en: THE SPACE: the body or group moves toward what lies ahead.
branches.cn: 空间线：身体或队伍朝前方移动。

branches.en: THE TIME: progress is forward movement measured in time.
branches.cn: 时间线：进展是用时间衡量的向前移动。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: something is pushed forward for others' benefit.
branches.cn: 事业线：某事物为他人利益被向前推动。

branches.en: THE MONEY: payment or booking is placed before the due moment.
branches.cn: 钱款线：付款或预订被放在到期时刻之前。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a theory is brought to the front for others to see.
branches.cn: 观点线：理论被带到前面供他人审视。

intro.en: Advance is an Old French verb resting on a Latin phrase, with English endings building the family.
intro.cn: advance 是一个建立在拉丁短语之上的古法语动词，英语后缀再扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin abante is a fixed phrase rather than a single root word; its parts ab- and ante are both recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abante 是一个固定短语而非单一词根，其组成 ab- 与 ante 均有记录。

items.example: It supplies the idea of being ahead.
It is the base of the Old French verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是古法语动词的基础。

items.example: It is the direct source of advance.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advance 的直接来源。

items.example: It survives in words such as antenatal.
items.exampleCN: 它保留在 antenatal 等词中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「推进；进步」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「先进的；高级的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「前进的」

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；益处；有利时机；（网球）占先
definition_en: a condition that puts someone in a better position, a benefit, or the tennis point after deuce
core_image: 棋盘上多出的一枚棋子，让一方先看到胜路
scene: 两支队伍实力接近，教练在赛前反复研究对方的弱点。Their greater experience gave them a clear advantage in the final.
sceneCN: 这里 advantage 是「优势」（第 1 个义项：使人处于更有利地位的条件）；句意为更丰富的经验让他们在决赛中占有明显优势。

pos.zh: 优势；有利条件；益处；占先

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「有利的」
由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有利地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利条件」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「处于有利地位的」

senses.title: A condition that puts one in a better position
senses.definition: something that gives a person or group a better chance of success than others
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或群体比他人更有成功机会的条件
senses.example: Their greater experience gave them a clear advantage in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 更丰富的经验让他们在决赛中占有明显优势。
senses.why: The Old French source meant a position in front, so an advantage is literally the front place.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为「处于前方的位置」，所以 advantage 字面上就是「前排的位置」。

senses.title: A benefit or profit
senses.definition: a useful or helpful effect that something brings
senses.definitionCN: 某事物带来的有用或有益效果
senses.example: One advantage of the new system is that it saves paper.
senses.exampleCN: 新系统的一个好处是节省纸张。
senses.why: Being ahead brings gains, so the front position also means the profit it yields.
senses.whyCN: 处在前面会带来收益，所以「前排位置」也指它带来的好处。

senses.title: A favourable opportunity
senses.definition: a good chance or opening that can be used
senses.definitionCN: 可以利用的良好机会或突破口
senses.example: The confusion gave the thief an advantage to slip away.
senses.exampleCN: 混乱给了小偷溜走的机会。
senses.why: A position in front creates a moment when action is easier, and that moment is the advantage.
senses.whyCN: 处在前面会造成一个行动更容易的时刻，这个时刻就是有利时机。

senses.title: To make use of, in take advantage of
senses.definition: in the phrase take advantage of, to use something or someone for one's own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 take advantage of，表示为自身利益利用某物或某人
senses.example: She took advantage of the quiet morning to finish her report.
senses.exampleCN: 她利用安静的清晨完成了报告。
senses.why: To take the advantage is to seize the front position and turn it into gain.
senses.whyCN: take the advantage 就是抢占前面的位置，并把它转化为收益。

senses.title: The point after deuce in tennis
senses.definition: in tennis, the first point scored after deuce, which gives the server or receiver the chance to win the game
senses.definitionCN: 网球中在平分后得到的第一分，使发球方或接球方有机会赢下这一局
senses.example: She held her advantage and served out the game.
senses.exampleCN: 她保住占先，并拿下了这一局。
senses.why: The scoring term borrows the same idea: one player is now one step in front of the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个计分术语借用同一想法：一方现在比另一方领先一步。

intro.en: Advantage and advance come from the same Old French idea of being in front.
intro.cn: advantage 与 advance 出自同一个古法语观念，即「处于前方」。

items.en: Ante meant before or in front of.
items.cn: ante 意为在……之前或前面。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened to benefit, opportunity, exploitation, and a tennis score.
items.cn: 词义扩展到好处、机会、利用以及网球计分。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the front-position root; the near-meaning group gathers benefits and margins.

entries.definition: Giving a benefit or a better position.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有利的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A condition that makes success harder.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不利条件」，由否定前缀加本词构成。

entries.definition: Having special benefits or a better position.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「处于有利地位的」。

entries.definition: To move forward; the verb behind the front position.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「前进」，与本词共享「在前」词源。

entries.definition: A helpful or positive effect.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「益处」，对应「好处」义项。

entries.definition: A slight advantage over another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微弱优势」，口语常用。

entries.definition: The state of being better or stronger than another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优越性」，强调胜过对方。

entries.definition: Something useful or valuable that one possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有利资源、资产」，指拥有的有价值之物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the front-position root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「前排位置」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Avant means before, so an advantage is the place in front.
normal.cn: avant 意为在前面，所以 advantage 就是前面的位置。

normal.en: The same root gives advance: to move to the front.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 advance，即移动到前面。

normal.en: Take advantage of means seize the front place for yourself.
normal.cn: take advantage of 意为把前面的位置据为己用。

normal.en: Having an advantage over someone is standing one step ahead.
normal.cn: have an advantage over 某人，就是比对方站前一步。

normal.en: In tennis, advantage is the point that puts one player ahead.
normal.cn: 在网球里，advantage 就是让一方领先的那一分。

abstract.en: One extra chess piece on the board.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上多出的一枚棋子。

abstract.en: A runner who starts half a step ahead of the line.
abstract.cn: 一名比起跑线多半步出发的跑者。

abstract.en: A key that opens a door before anyone else reaches it.
abstract.cn: 一把在他人到达之前就打开门的钥匙。

examples.en: The new bridge gives the town an advantage in trade.
examples.cn: 新桥让这座镇子在贸易上占有优势。

examples.en: One advantage of living here is the short commute.
examples.cn: 住在这里的一个好处是通勤时间短。

examples.en: They took advantage of the holiday to visit the coast.
examples.cn: 他们利用假期去了海边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one extra piece on the board lets one side see the win first.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上多出一枚棋子，让一方先看到胜路。

branches.en: THE POSITION: standing ahead gives a better chance.
branches.cn: 位置线：站在前面带来更好的机会。

branches.en: THE GAIN: the front place yields profit.
