definition_zh: 冒险；奇遇；冒险活动；风险事业
definition_en: an exciting and sometimes dangerous experience, or a risky journey or undertaking
core_image: 一张展开的地图，角落画着问号与风暴
scene: 年轻人背起行囊，没有详细计划就出发去山里。Their adventure in the mountains lasted three weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 adventure 是「冒险活动」（第 2 个义项：有风险的旅程）；句意为他们在山中的冒险持续了三周。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「爱冒险的；惊险的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「冒险者」
由 adventurous 加 -ly 构成，义为「冒险地」
由前缀 mis- 加本词构成，义为「不幸的遭遇」

senses.title: An exciting and unusual experience
senses.definition: an exciting, remarkable, and often slightly risky experience
senses.definitionCN: 令人兴奋、不寻常且常带一点风险的经历
senses.example: Meeting the old sailor was a strange adventure.
senses.exampleCN: 遇见那位老水手是一次奇特的经历。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'things about to happen', so an adventure is whatever comes next, especially if it surprises.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为「即将发生之事」，所以 adventure 就是接下来发生的事，尤其当它出人意料时。

senses.title: A risky journey or undertaking
senses.definition: a journey or project that involves danger, uncertainty, or the unknown
senses.definitionCN: 带有危险、不确定或未知因素的旅程或计划
senses.example: Their adventure in the mountains lasted three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山中的冒险持续了三周。
senses.why: A journey into the unknown is the noun at its fullest: a stretch of time given over to what may happen.
senses.whyCN: 进入未知的旅程是这个名词最完整的形态：一段交给「可能发生之事」的时间。

senses.title: A speculative business venture, in older use
senses.definition: in older commercial English, a business undertaking whose outcome is uncertain
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的商业英语中，结果不确定的商业计划
senses.example: The trading adventure lost most of its money.
senses.exampleCN: 那项贸易投机赔掉了大部分资金。
senses.why: Commerce borrowed the word for ventures whose outcome, like a journey, could not be known in advance.
senses.whyCN: 商业借用了这个词，指结果如同旅程一样无法预知的事业。

senses.title: To venture, in literary use
senses.definition: in literary English, to go into danger or the unknown
senses.definitionCN: 在文学英语中，进入危险或未知之地
senses.example: They adventured into unknown waters.
senses.exampleCN: 他们冒险驶入未知海域。
senses.why: The rare verb turns the noun into an act of entering what may happen.
senses.whyCN: 这个罕见的动词把名词变成「走进可能发生之事」的动作。

intro.en: Adventure comes from a Latin word for things about to happen, carried through Old French.
intro.cn: adventure 出自一个表示「即将发生之事」的拉丁词，经古法语传入英语。

items.en: Advenire meant to come to or arrive.
items.cn: advenire 意为来到、抵达。

items.en: Adventura meant things about to happen, or what will come.
items.cn: adventura 意为即将发生之事，或将要来临的事。

items.en: Old French aventure carried the sense of chance, fortune, and a risky happening.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 带有「机缘、命运、冒险之事」的意思。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense settled on exciting or dangerous experience and the journeys that produce it.
items.cn: 词义固定在令人兴奋或危险的经历，以及产生这些经历的旅程。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'what will happen' root; the near-meaning group gathers journeys and risky exploits.
note.cn: 形近组共享「将要发生之事」词根；近义组收旅程与冒险行为。

entries.definition: Willing to take risks and try new things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「爱冒险的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A person who seeks adventures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冒险者」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A risky undertaking; a shortened relative of adventure.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「风险事业；冒险」，是 adventure 的同源近亲。

entries.definition: An unlucky accident or mishap.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不幸遭遇」，由前缀 mis- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: An organized journey with a purpose, often to explore.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「远征、探险」，强调有组织的旅程。

entries.definition: A adventurous act that is slightly reckless or mischievous.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「越轨的冒险行为」，常带轻率或顽皮色彩。

entries.definition: A long search or journey toward a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「探索、追寻」，强调目标驱动的长途旅程。

entries.definition: The chance of danger or loss.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「风险」，是冒险的核心要素。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the 'things about to happen' root into journeys and ventures.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着「即将发生之事」词根，走向旅程与风险事业。

normal.en: Adventura means things about to happen, so adventure is whatever waits ahead.
normal.cn: adventura 意为即将发生之事，所以 adventure 就是前方等着的事。

normal.en: The same family gives venture, a risky undertaking.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 venture，即风险事业。

normal.en: An adventure story is built on the unknown around the next bend.
normal.cn: 冒险故事建立在下一个转弯处的未知。

normal.en: A sense of adventure is the willingness to meet what may happen.
normal.cn: sense of adventure 就是愿意迎接可能发生之事。

normal.en: Misadventure is the same word with a bad outcome attached.
normal.cn: misadventure 就是同一个词加上了不幸的结果。

abstract.en: A map with a question mark drawn in its corner.
abstract.cn: 一张在地图角落画着问号的地图。

abstract.en: A backpack waiting by the door before dawn.
abstract.cn: 黎明前等在门口的一只背包。

abstract.en: A road that disappears into mist.
abstract.cn: 一条消失在雾中的路。

examples.en: The trip turned into an adventure when the bus broke down.
examples.cn: 巴士抛锚后，这趟旅行变成了冒险。

examples.en: She wrote a book about her adventures at sea.
examples.cn: 她写了一本关于自己海上冒险的书。

examples.en: He has a real sense of adventure.
examples.cn: 他真有冒险精神。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文丘」——阿德把地图铺开，文丘（问球）般走向未知

root: 源自拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」，出自 advenire「来到、抵达」，由 ad-「向」加 venire「来」构成；古法语 aventure 带入英语。核心是「前方将要发生的事」，由此发展出「奇遇」「冒险旅程」「风险事业」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: an exciting experience, a risky journey, a speculative venture, and the rare verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：刺激的经历、风险旅程、投机事业，以及罕见的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open map with a storm and a question mark in one corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张摊开的地图，角落画着风暴与问号。

branches.en: THE EXPERIENCE: something unexpected arrives and becomes memorable.
branches.cn: 经历线：意外之事到来，并变得难忘。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: a stretch of time is given to the unknown.
branches.cn: 旅程线：一段时间被交给未知。

branches.en: THE VENTURE: commerce borrows the uncertainty of travel.
branches.cn: 事业线：商业借用了旅行的不确定性。

branches.en: THE ACT: the rare verb steps into what may happen.
branches.cn: 动作线：罕见的动词走进可能发生之事。

branches.en: THE STORY: experience and journey become the material of tales.
branches.cn: 故事线：经历与旅程成为传说的素材。

intro.en: Adventure joins a Latin prefix and a Latin verb of coming, then passes through Old French.
intro.cn: adventure 由一个拉丁前缀和一个表示「来」的拉丁动词构成，再经古法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin advenire and adventura are recorded, so the deeper origin of venire is the only uncertain part.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 advenire 与 adventura 均有记录，只有 venire 更早的来源不确定。

items.example: It directs the coming toward a place.
It is the source of the noun.
It is the model for adventure.
It carries the word to English.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ous 构成，义为「爱冒险的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「冒险者」
由 adventurous 加 -ly 构成，义为「冒险地」
由前缀 mis- 加本词构成，义为「不幸遭遇」

definition_zh: 副词；状语词
definition_en: a word that modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb, often showing how, when, or where
core_image: 一个小助手跟在动词身后，调整它的速度与方向
scene: 语法课上，老师把一个句子写在黑板上，圈出修饰动作的词。In the sentence, the adverb quickly tells us how the action was done.
sceneCN: 这里 adverb 是「副词」（第 1 个义项：修饰动词的词）；句意为在这个句子里，副词 quickly 告诉我们动作是怎样完成的。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「副词的；状语」
由 adverbial 加 -ly 构成，义为「作状语地」
由 adverbial 加 -ize 构成，义为「使副词化」

senses.title: A word that modifies a verb
senses.definition: a word that adds information about how, when, or where an action happens
senses.definitionCN: 补充动作发生方式、时间或地点信息的词
senses.example: In the sentence, the adverb quickly tells us how the action was done.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，副词 quickly 告诉我们动作是怎样完成的。
senses.why: The Latin name means 'added to a verb', so the word is defined by standing beside the verb.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名称意为「加在动词上」，所以这个词是由「站在动词旁边」来定义的。

senses.title: A word that modifies an adjective or another adverb
senses.titleCN: 修饰形容词或其他副词的副词
senses.definition: a word that changes the strength or quality of an adjective or another adverb
senses.definitionCN: 改变形容词或另一个副词的强度或性质的词
senses.example: The adverb very makes the adjective stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 副词 very 让那个形容词的程度更强。
senses.why: The name was extended from verbs to other modifiers, because the same kind of word does the same kind of work.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称从动词扩展到其他修饰语，因为同一类词做着同一类工作。

senses.title: The adverb as a word class
senses.definition: the grammatical category of words that mainly modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs
senses.definitionCN: 主要修饰动词、形容词或其他副词的语法类别
senses.example: Adverbs form one of the traditional parts of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 副词是传统词类之一。
senses.why: Grammar turns the individual word into a class, and the class keeps the old name.
senses.whyCN: 语法把单个词提升为一个类别，而类别沿用旧名。

senses.title: Any word or phrase doing an adverb's job
senses.definition: loosely, any word or phrase that functions like an adverb in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地说，任何在句中起副词作用的词或短语
senses.example: The phrase after lunch works as an adverb of time.
senses.exampleCN: 短语 after lunch 起时间副词的作用。
senses.why: Function matters more than form, so phrases can be treated as adverbs when they modify the action.
senses.whyCN: 功能比形式更重要，所以修饰动作的短语也可按副词看待。

intro.en: Adverb is a Latin loan translation: a word added to a verb.
intro.cn: adverb 是一个拉丁语仿译词，字面意思是「加在动词上的词」。

items.en: Verbum meant word, and later also verb.
items.cn: verbum 意为「词」，后来也指「动词」。

items.en: Adverbium meant a word added to a verb, modelled on the Greek term epirrhema.
items.cn: adverbium 意为加在动词上的词，是仿照希腊语 epirrhema 构成的。

items.en: Old French carried the grammatical term toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个语法术语带入英语。

items.en: The term is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个术语在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The term widened from words added to verbs to any modifier of a verb, adjective, or adverb.
items.cn: 这个术语从「加在动词上」扩展到修饰动词、形容词或副词的任何词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adverb family and its grammatical neighbours; the near-meaning group names modifier types.
note.cn: 形近组是 adverb 词族及其语法近邻；近义组收各类修饰成分。

entries.definition: Relating to an adverb, or a phrase that acts like one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「副词的；状语」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: In the manner of an adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「作状语地」，由 adverbial 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A word expressing an action or state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「动词」，是 adverb 这个术语所依附的词类。

entries.definition: A word that describes a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形容词」，与副词同属修饰语词类。

entries.definition: Any word or phrase that limits or describes another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修饰语」，是副词的上位概念。

entries.definition: An adverb that strengthens or weakens another word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强调成分」，如 very、quite 这类副词。

entries.definition: A word that links clauses or sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「连接成分」，与句子副词功能相邻。

entries.definition: A short unchanging word with grammatical function.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小品词」，部分副词性小词可归入此类。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal meaning 'added to a verb' and the grammatical family around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面意思「加在动词上」，以及周围的语法词族。

normal.en: Adverb literally means added to a verb, so it is the verb's helper.
normal.cn: adverb 字面意思是「加在动词上」，所以它是动词的助手。

normal.en: The Latin word was modelled on a Greek grammatical term.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁词是仿照一个希腊语法术语构成的。

normal.en: Adverbial is the adjective, and it also names a phrase that behaves like an adverb.
normal.cn: adverbial 是形容词，也指起副词作用的短语。

normal.en: Adverbs answer how, when, where, and how often.
normal.cn: 副词回答「怎样、何时、何地、多久一次」。

normal.en: Many adverbs end in -ly, but not all: fast and soon are adverbs too.
normal.cn: 许多副词以 -ly 结尾，但并非全部：fast 与 soon 也是副词。

abstract.en: A small figure walking beside a larger one, adjusting its pace.
abstract.cn: 一个小人走在大个子旁边，调整着他的步伐。

abstract.en: A dial on a machine that turns the action up or down.
abstract.cn: 机器上的一个旋钮，把动作调大或调小。

abstract.en: A shadow that tells you when and where the action happens.
abstract.cn: 一道影子，告诉你动作在何时何地发生。

examples.en: The adverb slowly describes the way he walked.
examples.cn: 副词 slowly 描述他走路的方式。

examples.en: Adverbs can modify adjectives as well as verbs.
examples.cn: 副词既能修饰动词，也能修饰形容词。

examples.en: Put the adverb before the main verb in this sentence.
examples.cn: 在这个句子里，把副词放在主动词之前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃布」——阿德在动词旁边加了个「沃布」（小助手）

root: 源自拉丁语 adverbium，字面意为「加在动词上的词」，是仿照希腊语 epirrhema 构成的语法术语；由 ad-「向、加于」加 verbum「词、动词」构成。核心是「附着在动词旁边的修饰词」，后来扩展到修饰形容词与其他副词。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: modifying a verb, modifying other modifiers, the word class, and any adverbial element.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：修饰动词、修饰其他修饰语、副词词类，以及任何状语性成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small helper walks beside a verb and adjusts its speed and direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小助手走在动词旁边，调整它的速度与方向。

branches.en: THE VERB: the helper tells how the action happens.
branches.cn: 动词线：助手说明动作怎样发生。

branches.en: THE OTHER MODIFIER: the same helper strengthens an adjective or another adverb.
branches.cn: 其他修饰语线：同一助手加强形容词或另一个副词。

branches.en: THE CLASS: grammar gathers all such words under one name.
branches.cn: 词类线：语法把所有这类词归入一个名称。

branches.en: THE FUNCTION: a phrase can do the same job as one word.
branches.cn: 功能线：短语也能完成单词同样的工作。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTMENT: whether beside a verb or adjective, the role is to modify.
branches.cn: 调整线：无论跟在动词还是形容词旁，角色都是修饰。

intro.en: Adverb is a Latin compound of 'to' and 'word', used as a grammatical label.
intro.cn: adverb 是拉丁语「向」与「词」的复合词，用作语法标签。

latinIntro.en: Latin verbum and adverbium are recorded; the Greek model epirrhema is also attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verbum 与 adverbium 均有记录，希腊语范本 epirrhema 也有文献。

items.example: It marks the word as added to another.
items.exampleCN: 它标出这个词是加在另一个词上的。

items.example: It is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它是复合词的后半部分。

items.example: It is the direct source of adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adverb 的直接来源。

items.example: It was the model for the Latin term.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个拉丁术语的范本。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「副词的；状语」
由 adverbial 加 -ly 构成，义为「作状语地」
由 adverbial 加 -ize 构成，义为「使副词化」

definition_zh: 对手；敌手；敌人；（法庭上的）对方
definition_en: a person or group that opposes another in a contest, conflict, or legal case
core_image: 两个人隔着棋盘对坐，目光都盯着对方的王
scene: 赛前新闻发布会上，两队教练都刻意避免提到对方的名字。The champion faced a determined adversary in the final round.
sceneCN: 这里 adversary 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：比赛中的对方）；句意为冠军在最后一轮遇到一个顽强的对手。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「对抗性的」
由 adversarial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以对抗方式」
由 adversarial 加 -ness 构成，义为「对抗性」

senses.title: An opponent in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team that competes against another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方竞争的人或队伍
senses.example: The champion faced a determined adversary in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军在最后一轮遇到一个顽强的对手。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'turned against', so an adversary is someone whose face is turned toward you in opposition.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「转向对立面」，所以对手就是面对面与你相对的人。

senses.title: An enemy in a conflict
senses.definition: a person or group actively hostile in a struggle or war
senses.definitionCN: 在斗争或战争中主动敌对的个人或群体
senses.example: The two countries had been adversaries for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个国家几十年来一直是敌手。
senses.why: Contest and conflict share the same structure: two sides turned against each other.
senses.whyCN: 竞争与冲突结构相同：两方彼此转向对立。

senses.title: The opposing side in a legal case
senses.definition: the opposing party in a legal proceeding, often used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 法律程序中的对方当事人，常置于名词前作定语
senses.example: The case was decided in an adversary proceeding.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案件在对抗式程序中得到裁决。
senses.why: Law treats the two parties as opponents facing each other across the courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 法律把双方当事人当作在法庭两端相对的对手。

intro.en: Adversary comes from a Latin word for an opponent, built on the verb 'to turn'.
intro.cn: adversary 出自一个表示「对手」的拉丁词，其基础是「转」这个动词。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」。

items.en: Adversus meant turned toward or turned against.
items.cn: adversus 意为转向、转为对立。

items.en: Adversarius named a person who stands opposed to another.
items.cn: adversarius 指站在他人对立面的人。

items.en: Old French carried the noun toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from a contestant to an enemy and to the opposing party in law.
items.cn: 词义从比赛对手扩展到敌人，再扩展到法律上的对方当事人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'turn against' root; the near-meaning group gathers opponents and enemies.
note.cn: 形近组共享「转向对立」词根；近义组收对手与敌人。

entries.definition: Unfavourable or harmful; literally turned against.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不利的」，字面即「转为对立」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A difficult or unlucky situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逆境」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Characterized by opposition or conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「对抗性的」，由本词加 -ial 构成。

entries.definition: Strongly disliking something; from the same verb of turning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反感的」，出自同一「转」动词，属同根但用法不同。

entries.definition: A person who competes against another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「对手」，是最中性的对应词。

entries.definition: A person or group competing for the same goal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「竞争者」，强调争夺同一目标。

entries.definition: A person or group actively hostile to another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敌人」，敌意最强。

entries.definition: An enemy, used mainly in literary or formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敌人」，多用于文学或正式文本。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real 'turn against' root and the contest, war, and courtroom settings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用真实的「转向对立」词根，以及比赛、战争与法庭三个场景。

normal.en: Vertere means to turn, so an adversary is someone turned against you.
normal.cn: vertere 意为转，所以对手就是转向你对立面的人。

normal.en: Adverse and adversity share the same root: what is turned against you.
normal.cn: adverse 与 adversity 同根：转向你、与你作对之物。

normal.en: In a contest, the adversary is the other side of the board.
normal.cn: 在比赛中，对手就是棋盘对面的那一方。

normal.en: In law, the adversary is the opposing party across the courtroom.
normal.cn: 在法律中，对手就是法庭另一端的对方当事人。

normal.en: A worthy adversary is one who makes the contest better.
normal.cn: a worthy adversary 指让比赛更精彩的对手。

abstract.en: Two chairs facing each other across a chessboard.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子隔着棋盘相对而放。

abstract.en: Two flags on opposite hills.
abstract.cn: 两面旗子插在对望的山头。

abstract.en: A door that opens only toward one person.
abstract.cn: 一扇只朝一个人方向打开的门。

examples.en: She defeated a much younger adversary in the final.
examples.cn: 她在决赛中击败了一个年轻得多的对手。

examples.en: The two leaders had been adversaries for years.
examples.cn: 这两位领导人多年来一直是敌手。

examples.en: The lawyer studied the adversary's arguments.
examples.cn: 律师研究了对方的论点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃瑟里」——阿德把椅子转向对面，与沃瑟里对峙

root: 源自拉丁语 adversarius「对手」，出自 adversus「转向、对立」，而 adversus 又出自 vertere「转」；古法语 adversaire 带入英语。核心是「转过身来与你相对」，由此发展出「比赛对手」「敌人」「法庭上的对方」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the contestant, the enemy, and the opposing party in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：比赛对手、敌人、法律上的对方当事人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people sit across a board, each watching the other's king.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔着棋盘对坐，各自盯着对方的王。

branches.en: THE BOARD: the other player competes for the same win.
branches.cn: 棋盘线：另一位玩家争夺同一场胜利。

branches.en: THE WAR: hostility turns the contest into enmity.
branches.cn: 战争线：敌意把竞争变成敌对。

branches.en: THE COURT: two parties face each other in law.
branches.cn: 法庭线：双方在法律上彼此相对。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: opposition is formal in both game and law.
branches.cn: 结构线：无论游戏还是法律，对立都是形式化的。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: whether enemy or opposing party, the figure is defined from the opposite side.
branches.cn: 对方线：无论敌人还是对方当事人，这个身份都由对立面定义。

intro.en: Adversary is built on the Latin verb 'to turn', with direction and a person suffix.
intro.cn: adversary 建立在拉丁语「转」这个动词上，加上方向与表示人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, adversus and adversarius are recorded, so the family is well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere、adversus 与 adversarius 均有记录，这一词族文献充分。

items.example: It directs the turning toward someone.
It is the direct source of adversary.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adversary 的直接来源。

由 adversarial 加 -ly 构成，义为「以对抗方式」

definition_zh: 不利的；有害的；相反的；敌对的
definition_en: unfavourable, harmful, or opposed in direction or attitude
core_image: 帆船遇上逆风，船头被推得偏了方向
scene: 天气预报说夜里有大风，果农连夜给幼苗搭起挡风墙。The crop suffered from adverse weather for two weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 adverse 是「不利的」（第 1 个义项：造成困难或损害）；句意为庄稼连续两周受到不利天气的影响。

pos.zh: 不利的；有害的；相反的；敌对的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」
由同一词根 adversus 加 -ity 构成，义为「逆境」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「不利；对立」
由同一词根 adversarius 构成，义为「对手」

senses.title: Unfavourable or harmful
senses.definition: causing difficulty, damage, or a worse chance of success
senses.definitionCN: 造成困难、损害或降低成功机会
senses.example: The crop suffered from adverse weather for two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 庄稼连续两周受到不利天气的影响。
senses.why: The root means turned against, so adverse conditions are conditions that work against you.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「转为对立」，所以不利条件就是与你作对的条件。

senses.title: Opposing or contrary in direction
senses.definition: moving or pointing in the opposite direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝相反方向移动或指向
senses.example: They sailed against an adverse wind for the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个下午都顶着逆风航行。
senses.why: A wind turned against the ship is the literal picture behind the figurative sense.
senses.whyCN: 风转为与船相对，正是这一比喻义背后的字面画面。

senses.title: Unwanted, as in a medical reaction
senses.definition: unwanted and harmful, used especially of reactions to drugs or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 不想要且有害的，尤指对药物或治疗的反应
senses.example: Some patients reported adverse reactions to the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 一些病人报告了对该药物的不良反应。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the word for effects that turn against the body rather than help it.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用这个词，指那些与身体作对而非帮助身体的效果。

senses.title: Hostile or critical in attitude
senses.definition: hostile or strongly critical, as in adverse criticism or an adverse report
senses.definitionCN: 敌对或强烈批评的，如敌意批评或不利报告
senses.example: The plan drew adverse criticism from local residents.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划招致当地居民的批评。
senses.why: People turned against an idea produce comment that is likewise turned against it.
senses.whyCN: 人们转而反对某个想法，产生的评论也就同样与之对立。

intro.en: Adverse is the participle of the Latin verb 'to turn', meaning turned against.
intro.cn: adverse 是拉丁语「转」这个动词的分词，意为「转为对立」。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」。

items.en: Adversus meant turned toward or turned against, and was used of winds and fortune.
items.cn: adversus 意为转向、转为对立，常用于风与命运。

items.en: Adversitas named opposition and misfortune.
items.cn: adversitas 指对立与不幸。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense widened from contrary winds to harmful conditions, medical reactions, and hostile criticism.
items.cn: 词义从逆风扩展到有害条件、医学反应与敌意批评。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'turn against' root; the near-meaning group gathers harmful and opposing adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组共享「转向对立」词根；近义组收有害与相反类形容词。

entries.definition: An opponent or enemy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「对手、敌人」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A difficult or unlucky situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逆境」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Strongly disliking something; note the different ending and use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反感的」，与 adverse 形近但搭配不同，多用 be averse to。

entries.definition: In a harmful or unfavourable way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不利地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Not helpful or likely to bring success.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不利的」，是最直接的近义词。

entries.definition: Causing damage or injury.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」，强调造成损害。

entries.definition: Unfriendly and opposed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「敌对的」，对应态度义项。

entries.definition: Opposite in direction or nature.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「相反的」，对应方向义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal wind image and the word's modern extensions.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面上的逆风意象，以及这个词的现代扩展义。

normal.en: Adverse literally means turned against, like a wind against a ship.
normal.cn: adverse 字面意为「转为对立」，像逆风吹向船只。

normal.en: An adverse effect is an effect that works against you.
normal.cn: adverse effect 就是与你作对的效果。

normal.en: An adverse reaction is the body turning against a drug.
normal.cn: adverse reaction 就是身体对药物产生对抗。

normal.en: Adverse criticism is criticism turned against the plan.
normal.cn: adverse criticism 就是针对计划的敌意批评。

normal.en: Do not confuse adverse with averse: one is against you, the other is your dislike.
normal.cn: 不要把 adverse 与 averse 混淆：前者与你作对，后者是你的反感。

abstract.en: A sail bent by wind blowing the wrong way.
abstract.cn: 一张被反方向的风吹弯的帆。

abstract.en: A door that pushes back when you try to open it.
abstract.cn: 一扇你越推、它越往回顶的门。

abstract.en: A road sign pointing the opposite way to your destination.
abstract.cn: 一块指向你目的地反方向的指示牌。

examples.en: Adverse conditions delayed the flight.
examples.cn: 不利条件使航班延误。

examples.en: The medicine can have adverse effects on the liver.
examples.cn: 这种药可能对肝脏产生不利影响。

examples.en: The proposal met with adverse comments.
examples.cn: 这项提议遭到了反对意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃斯」——阿德逆着风走，越走越不利

root: 源自拉丁语 adversus「转向、对立」，是 vertere「转」的过去分词；古法语 avers 带入英语。核心意象是「风转为与船相对」，由此发展出「不利的」「有害的」「逆向的」「敌意的」「医学上不良反应的」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: unfavourable conditions, contrary direction, unwanted medical effects, and hostile criticism.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：不利条件、相反方向、医学上的不良反应、敌意批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sailboat meets a headwind and its bow is pushed off course.
core.cn: 核心意象：帆船遇到逆风，船头被推离航向。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: what works against you makes success harder.
branches.cn: 条件线：与你作对之物让成功更难。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: wind or force points the other way.
branches.cn: 方向线：风或力指向相反方向。

branches.en: THE BODY: a drug's effect turns against the patient.
branches.cn: 身体线：药效转为与病人作对。

branches.en: THE VOICE: critics turn against the plan.
branches.cn: 声音线：批评者转而反对计划。

branches.en: THE RESISTANCE: harm and opposite direction share one image of pushback.
branches.cn: 阻力线：损害与相反方向共享同一个「回推」意象。

intro.en: Adverse is a Latin participle with a prefix of direction, used directly as an English adjective.
intro.cn: adverse 是一个带方向前缀的拉丁分词，直接用作英语形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere, adversus and adversitas are recorded, so the family is well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere、adversus 与 adversitas 均有记录，词族文献充分。

items.example: It directs the turning toward something.
It is the direct source of adverse.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adverse 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the model for adversity.
It forms averse, a close but differently used word.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 averse，一个形近但用法不同的词。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」
由同一词根加 -ity 构成，义为「逆境」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「不利；对立」
由同一词根 adversarius 构成，义为「对手」

definition_zh: 为……做广告；宣传；公告；登广告招聘
definition_en: to promote goods or services publicly, to make something known, or to call attention to something
core_image: 街角的招牌转着圈，把商品的名字送进每个路人的耳朵
scene: 小店开业前，店主把彩色海报贴满了附近的公告栏。They advertised the new shop on every notice board in town.
sceneCN: 这里 advertise 是「为……做广告」（第 1 个义项：公开宣传商品或服务）；句意为他们在镇上每块公告栏上为新店做广告。

pos.zh: 做广告；宣传；公告；登广告招聘

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「广告主」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」
英式英语中由本词缩略而来，义为「广告」

senses.title: To promote goods or services publicly
senses.definition: to draw public attention to goods, services, or an event in order to sell or promote them
senses.definitionCN: 为销售或推广而把商品、服务或活动引入公众注意
senses.example: They advertised the new shop on every notice board in town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在镇上每块公告栏上为新店做广告。
senses.why: The Latin source means to turn attention toward something, which is exactly what an advertisement does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为「把注意力转向某物」，这正是广告所做的事。

senses.title: To make something publicly known
senses.definition: to make a fact, event, or intention known to the public
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事实、事件或意图公开告知公众
senses.example: The committee advertised the date of the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会公布了会议日期。
senses.why: Before selling, advertise simply meant to give notice, and that older sense remains.
senses.whyCN: 在用于销售之前，advertise 只意为「发出通知」，这个较老的意思仍保留。

senses.title: To call attention to something, often unintentionally
senses.definition: to make a fact or quality conspicuous, sometimes without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事实或特点显眼，有时并非有意
senses.example: He advertised his ignorance by arguing too loudly.
senses.exampleCN: 他争吵得太大声音，反而暴露了自己的无知。
senses.why: If attention is drawn to something, it becomes visible whether you want it or not.
senses.whyCN: 注意力一旦被引向某物，无论你是否愿意，它都会变得显眼。

senses.title: To seek someone or something by advertising
senses.titleCN: 登广告招聘；登广告寻求
senses.definition: to place a notice in order to find a person, item, or opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 刊登启事以寻找某人、某物或某个机会
senses.example: The school advertised for a new music teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 学校登广告招聘一位新的音乐老师。
senses.why: A notice is turned toward the public so that the right person will answer it.
senses.whyCN: 启事被转向公众，好让合适的人来回应。

intro.en: Advertise comes from a Latin verb meaning to turn attention toward something.
intro.cn: advertise 出自一个意为「把注意力转向某物」的拉丁动词。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」。

items.en: Advertere meant to turn toward, and so to notice or attend to.
items.cn: advertere 意为转向，因此有「注意到、留意」之意。

items.en: Avertir meant to warn or notify, carrying the sense of drawing attention.
items.cn: avertir 意为警告或通知，带有「引人注意」的意思。

items.en: The verb entered English first as 'to give notice'; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词最初以「发出通知」义进入英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Commerce narrowed the everyday sense to promoting goods, while the notice sense survived in formal use.
items.cn: 商业把日常义收窄为推销商品，而「通知」义在正式用法中保留。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advertise family; the near-meaning group gathers promotion and announcement verbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 advertise 这一族词；近义组收推广与公告类动词。

entries.definition: A public notice promoting goods or services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: A person or company that advertises.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告主」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: The activity or industry of promoting products.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广告活动；广告业」。

entries.definition: A British shortening of advertisement.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语中 advertisement 的缩略形式。

entries.definition: To help sell or make something popular.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推广、促销」，侧重点在让产品更受欢迎。

entries.definition: To make something widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣传、公布」，侧重点在广为人知。

entries.definition: To state something publicly for the first time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布」，强调首次公开说明。

entries.definition: To promote and sell a product systematically.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「营销」，强调系统性的推广与销售。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the 'turn attention' root from a notice to a sales poster.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「转注意力」词根，从一纸通知走到销售海报。

normal.en: Advertere means turn toward, so advertise is turning the public's eyes toward something.
normal.cn: advertere 意为转向，所以 advertise 就是把公众的目光转向某物。

normal.en: An advertisement is the thing that does the turning.
normal.cn: advertisement 就是执行这个「转」的东西。

normal.en: To advertise for staff is to turn a notice toward possible workers.
normal.cn: advertise for staff 就是把启事转向可能的应聘者。

normal.en: A widely advertised sale is one many eyes have been turned toward.
normal.cn: a widely advertised sale 就是许多目光被引向的促销。

normal.en: You can advertise your ignorance without meaning to.
normal.cn: 你可能无意中就 advertise 了自己的无知。

abstract.en: A spinning sign at a street corner.
abstract.cn: 街角一块不停旋转的招牌。

abstract.en: A spotlight moved from an empty stage to a product.
abstract.cn: 一束聚光灯从空舞台移到一件商品上。

abstract.en: A hundred eyes turning at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 一百双眼睛在同一刻转过来。

examples.en: The company advertised its new phone on television.
examples.cn: 公司在电视上为新品手机做广告。

examples.en: They advertised the job in a local newspaper.
examples.cn: 他们在当地报纸上刊登了这个职位。

examples.en: The museum advertised the exhibition widely.
examples.cn: 博物馆广泛宣传了这场展览。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃泰兹」——阿德把招牌一转，路人的目光全被吸引

root: 源自拉丁语 advertere「转向、注意到」，由 ad-「向」加 vertere「转」构成；经古法语 avertir「通知」进入英语。核心是「把注意力转向某物」，由此发展出「做广告」「公开公告」「引人注意」「登广告招聘」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: promoting goods, giving public notice, drawing unwanted attention, and advertising a vacancy.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：推销商品、公开公告、引人注意（常非本意）、登广告招聘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spinning corner sign sends a product's name into every passer-by's ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角旋转的招牌把商品名字送进每个路人的耳朵。

branches.en: THE MARKET: attention is turned toward goods for sale.
branches.cn: 市场线：注意力被转向待售商品。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: a fact is turned toward the public.
branches.cn: 公告线：事实被转向公众。

branches.en: THE EXPOSURE: whatever attention lands on becomes visible.
branches.cn: 暴露线：注意力落到哪里，哪里就显眼。

branches.en: THE SEARCH: a notice turns toward the person being sought.
branches.cn: 寻找线：启事转向被寻找的人。

branches.en: THE PUBLICITY: selling and announcing share one act of turning.
branches.cn: 公开线：销售与公告共享同一个「转」的动作。

intro.en: Advertise is a Latin prefix and a Latin verb of turning, carried through Old French and extended by English suffixes.
intro.cn: advertise 由一个拉丁前缀和一个表示「转」的拉丁动词构成，经古法语传入并由英语后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere and advertere are recorded; the Old French verb avertir is the immediate source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 与 advertere 均有记录，古法语动词 avertir 是直接来源。

items.example: It directs the turning toward the public.
It is the immediate source of advertise.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advertise 的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the British spelling variants.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「广告主」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业」
英式英语中由本词缩略而来，义为「广告」

definition_zh: 建议；忠告；意见；（正式）通知
definition_en: an opinion or recommendation about what someone should do, or a formal notice
core_image: 一封写满提醒的信，被递到即将出发的人手里
scene: 朋友要签一份合同，却拿不准其中的条款。She asked a lawyer for advice before signing the contract.
sceneCN: 这里 advice 是「建议、意见」（第 1 个义项：关于该怎么做的意见）；句意为签合同前她向律师征求意见。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词源构成，义为「建议；通知」
由 advise 加 -able 构成，义为「明智的」
由 advise 加 -er 构成，义为「顾问」
由 advise 加 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；公告」

senses.title: An opinion about what someone should do
senses.definition: an opinion or recommendation offered to help someone decide or act
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助某人作决定或行动而提出的意见或推荐
senses.example: She asked a lawyer for advice before signing the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 签合同前她向律师征求意见。
senses.why: The Old French source means 'opinion', and an opinion offered for another's decision is advice.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为「意见」，而为他人的决定提供的意见就是建议。

senses.title: A formal notice, especially in trade
senses.definition: a formal notification, especially about a shipment, payment, or delivery
senses.definitionCN: 正式通知，尤指关于货运、付款或交付的通知
senses.example: The bank sent an advice of the transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行发来了一份转账通知。
senses.why: Commercial language kept the older sense of 'notice', which the everyday word has largely lost.
senses.whyCN: 商业语言保留了较老的「通知」义，而日常用语已基本不用它。

senses.title: Guidance as a body of recommendations
senses.definition: the collected recommendations given by an expert or authority
senses.definitionCN: 由专家或权威给出的成体系意见
senses.example: The report offers advice on how to save energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告就能源节约给出了指导意见。
senses.why: When many suggestions are gathered, advice becomes an uncountable body of guidance.
senses.whyCN: 当许多建议被汇集起来，advice 就成为一种不可数的指导意见。

intro.en: Advice comes from an Old French word for opinion, rooted in the Latin verb 'to see'.
intro.cn: advice 出自一个意为「意见」的古法语词，根源是拉丁语「看」这个动词。

items.en: Videre meant to see.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」。

items.en: Visum meant seen, or a thing that seems good after looking.
items.cn: visum 意为「所见的」，或经过观察后觉得好的东西。

items.en: Avis meant opinion or view, literally something seen.
items.cn: avis 意为意见或看法，字面是「所见之物」。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the thirteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十三世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Everyday use kept the sense of guidance, while commerce kept the sense of formal notice.
items.cn: 日常用法保留「指导」义，商业则保留「正式通知」义。

note.en: The look-alike group contains the classic advice and advise pair; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of guidance.
note.cn: 形近组包含经典的 advice / advise 一对；近义组收各类指导意见。

entries.definition: To give advice; the verb form, spelt with s.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，与名词 advice 同源，拼写以 s 结尾，是常考的形近对。

entries.definition: Sensible or recommended.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的、可取的」，由 advise 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A person who gives advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，由 advise 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Giving advice rather than making decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「咨询的；公告」，由 advise 加 -ory 构成。

entries.definition: An idea offered for consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建议」，语气比 advice 轻，只是供考虑。

entries.definition: A formal suggestion that something is worth doing or choosing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推荐、建议」，常较正式。

entries.definition: Advice, especially serious or professional advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「忠告」，语气正式，多指专业意见。

entries.definition: Help and direction given over time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「指导」，强调持续的引导。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the 'seen opinion' root and the spelling contrast with the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「所见的意见」词根，以及它与动词的拼写对比。

normal.en: Avis means opinion, literally something seen, so advice is a view offered to another.
normal.cn: avis 意为意见，字面是「看到的东西」，所以 advice 是提供给他人的看法。

normal.en: Advice is the noun with c; advise is the verb with s.
normal.cn: advice 是以 c 结尾的名词，advise 是以 s 结尾的动词。

normal.en: A piece of advice is one single suggestion.
normal.cn: a piece of advice 指一条建议。

normal.en: Legal advice is a professional opinion, not a casual chat.
normal.cn: legal advice 是专业意见，不是闲聊。

normal.en: In trade, an advice note is a formal notice of a shipment.
normal.cn: 在贸易中，advice note 是货运的正式通知单。

abstract.en: A letter passed into a traveller's hand just before departure.
abstract.cn: 一封信在出发前一刻被递到旅人手中。

abstract.en: A lamp held up so another can see the path.
abstract.cn: 一盏举起来的灯，让别人看清路。

abstract.en: Two spellings standing side by side, one noun, one verb.
abstract.cn: 两个拼写并排而立，一个是名词，一个是动词。

examples.en: Let me give you a piece of advice.
examples.cn: 我给你一条建议。

examples.en: She took her doctor's advice and rested.
examples.cn: 她听从医生的建议休息了。

examples.en: The company sent an advice of the payment.
examples.cn: 公司发了一份付款通知。

root: 源自拉丁语 visum「所见的」，出自 videre「看」，经古法语 avis「意见、看法」进入英语。核心是「看过之后形成的看法」，由此发展出「建议、忠告、意见」，并在商业文书中保留「正式通知」义。注意名词 advice 以 c 结尾，动词 advise 以 s 结尾。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a recommendation, a formal trade notice, and a body of expert guidance.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：建议、商业正式通知、成体系的专家指导。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a letter full of reminders is handed to someone about to leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：一封写满提醒的信，被递给即将出发的人。

branches.en: THE DECISION: a view is offered to help someone choose.
branches.cn: 决定线：看法被提供出来帮助他人选择。

branches.en: THE TRADE: the old sense of notice survives in commerce.
branches.cn: 贸易线：较老的「通知」义在商业中保留。

branches.en: THE BODY: many suggestions become a body of guidance.
branches.cn: 体系线：许多建议汇成一套指导意见。

branches.en: THE GUIDANCE: whether one tip or many, the aim is to direct action.
branches.cn: 指导线：无论一条还是多条，目的都是引导行动。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: written advice can be either guidance or a formal notice.
branches.cn: 文书线：书面 advice 既可以是指导，也可以是正式通知。

intro.en: Advice is an Old French noun from the Latin verb 'to see', with English suffixes building its family.
intro.cn: advice 是一个源自拉丁语「看」动词的古法语名词，英语后缀扩展出它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visum are recorded; the Old French noun avis is the immediate source of advice.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有记录，古法语名词 avis 是 advice 的直接来源。

items.example: It underlies the idea of an opinion.
items.exampleCN: 它是「意见」这一观念的基础。

items.example: It is the immediate source of advice.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advice 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms advices in trade use.
items.exampleCN: 它在商业用法中构成 advices。

items.example: It appears in the related verb advise.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在相关动词 advise 中。

由 advise 加 -able 构成，义为「明智的」

definition_zh: 明智的；可取的；适当的；建议采用的
definition_en: sensible or proper to do in the circumstances, or recommended by an authority
core_image: 岔路口一块牌子，箭头指向更安全的那条路
scene: 山路开始起雾，向导看了看天色，建议队伍掉头。It is advisable to turn back before the fog gets thicker.
sceneCN: 这里 advisable 是「明智的、可取的」（第 1 个义项：在特定情况下应当做）；句意为在雾变浓之前掉头是明智的。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「建议；通知」
由同一词源构成，义为「建议」
由 advisable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可取性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「明智地」

senses.title: Sensible or wise in the circumstances
senses.definition: sensible and likely to produce a good result in the situation at hand
senses.definitionCN: 在眼前情形中明智、且很可能带来好结果
senses.example: It is advisable to turn back before the fog gets thicker.
senses.exampleCN: 在雾变浓之前掉头是明智的。
senses.why: The suffix -able turns advise into 'worth being advised or recommended', so advisable describes what a sensible adviser would suggest.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把 advise 变成「值得被建议的」，所以 advisable 描述明智的顾问会推荐的做法。

senses.title: Recommended by an authority or professional
senses.titleCN: 建议采用的；合乎专业意见的
senses.definition: recommended as proper by a person or body with expert or official authority
senses.definitionCN: 由具有专业或官方权威的人或机构推荐为妥当
senses.example: Early testing is advisable for anyone with symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何有症状的人来说，尽早检测是可取的做法。
senses.why: What professionals advise becomes advisable, because the word points back to the advice behind it.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士建议的事就成为 advisable，因为这个词回指它背后的建议。

senses.title: Open to advice, in older use
senses.definition: in older English, willing to receive advice; now rare and usually replaced by other words
senses.definitionCN: 在较早英语中，愿意接受劝告；现已罕见，通常用别的词表达
senses.example: The old lord was advisable and changed his plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老领主愿意听劝，改变了自己的计划。
senses.why: The suffix once meant 'able to be advised', before the modern sense of 'worth recommending' took over.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀一度表示「能够被劝告」，后来才被现代义「值得推荐」取代。

intro.en: Advisable is advise plus -able, so its history is the history of advise.
intro.cn: advisable 是 advise 加 -able，所以它的历史就是 advise 的历史。

items.en: Videre meant to see, the deepest root of the family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，是这一词族最深的根。

items.en: Avis meant opinion or view.
items.cn: avis 意为意见或看法。

items.en: The verb advise entered English with the sense of giving an opinion.
items.cn: 动词 advise 以「给出意见」义进入英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded later, built with -able; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词较晚出现，由 -able 构成；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The modern sense settled on 'worth recommending', while the older 'open to advice' sense faded.
items.cn: 现代义固定在「值得推荐」，较老的「愿意听劝」义逐渐消失。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advise family; the near-meaning group gathers words for wise and recommended action.
note.cn: 形近组是 advise 这一族词；近义组收明智与被推荐的说法。

entries.definition: To give advice; the verb with s.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，以 s 结尾，是本词的基础。

entries.definition: An opinion about what to do; the noun with c.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建议」，以 c 结尾，与本词同源。

entries.definition: The quality of being advisable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可取性」，由本词加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: A person who gives advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，由 advise 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Based on good judgment; practical and wise.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的」，强调良好判断。

entries.definition: Careful and wise about the future.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谨慎的」，强调为将来打算。

entries.definition: Suggested as good or proper.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被推荐的」，对应权威建议义项。

entries.definition: Showing experience and good judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的」，最宽泛的对应词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the adjective from advise and its suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 advise 及其后缀出发，拼出这个形容词。

normal.en: Advisable is advise plus -able: worth being advised.
normal.cn: advisable 是 advise 加 -able：值得被建议的。

normal.en: It is advisable to do something means a sensible adviser would tell you to do it.
normal.cn: 「It is advisable to do something」意为明智的顾问会建议你这么做。

normal.en: Highly advisable is a stronger way to say very sensible.
normal.cn: highly advisable 是「非常明智」的更强说法。

normal.en: Not advisable is a polite way to say don't do it.
normal.cn: not advisable 是「别这么做」的委婉说法。

normal.en: The noun advice uses c, the verb advise uses s, and advisable keeps the s of the verb.
normal.cn: 名词 advice 用 c，动词 advise 用 s，而 advisable 保留动词的 s。

abstract.en: A sign at a fork pointing to the safer path.
abstract.cn: 岔路口一块指向更安全小路的牌子。

abstract.en: A hand gently turning a traveller away from the cliff.
abstract.cn: 一只手轻轻把旅人从悬崖边转开。

abstract.en: A lamp placed ahead so the next step is visible.
abstract.cn: 一盏放在前方的灯，让下一步看得清。

examples.en: It is advisable to book in advance.
examples.cn: 提前订票是可取的。

examples.en: Exercise is advisable for most patients.
examples.cn: 对多数病人来说，运动是明智的。

examples.en: Early application is strongly advisable.
examples.cn: 尽早申请是非常可取的。

root: 由动词 advise 加后缀 -able 构成。advise 源自拉丁语 visum「所见的」，出自 videre「看」，经古法语 avis「意见」进入英语。核心是「值得被建议的」，因此 advisable 表示「明智的、可取的、建议采用的」；较早还曾有「愿意听劝的」义，现已罕见。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: wise in the situation, recommended by authority, and the older sense of being open to advice.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：在当下明智、受权威推荐，以及较老的「愿意听劝」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fork in the road and a sign pointing toward the safer way.
core.cn: 核心意象：岔路口一块指向更安全道路的牌子。

branches.en: THE SITUATION: the wise choice depends on the circumstances.
branches.cn: 情境线：明智的选择取决于当下情形。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: professional advice makes an action advisable.
branches.cn: 权威线：专业建议使某项行动成为可取。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: an older word for being willing to take advice.
branches.cn: 旧义线：较早表示「愿意接受劝告」的用法。

branches.en: THE RECOMMENDATION: what is wise and what is advised point the same way.
branches.cn: 推荐线：明智之事与被建议之事指向同一方向。

branches.en: THE POSTURE: taking advice and giving advice meet in one word.
branches.cn: 姿态线：听劝与进言在同一个词中相遇。

intro.en: Advisable is an English verb plus the adjective suffix -able; the verb itself is Latin through Old French.
intro.cn: advisable 是一个英语动词加形容词后缀 -able；动词本身经古法语源自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visum are recorded; the suffix -able is English and fully productive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visum 均有记录，后缀 -able 是英语中能产的后缀。

definition_zh: 建议；劝告；通知；（专业上）为……提供意见
definition_en: to tell someone what you think they should do, or to inform someone formally
core_image: 一位老医生俯身向病人说明该怎样服药
scene: 年轻职员第一次处理客户投诉，不知道该先做什么。Her manager advised her to listen before answering.
sceneCN: 这里 advise 是「建议、劝告」（第 1 个义项：告诉某人该怎么做）；句意为经理建议她先听完再回答。

pos.zh: 建议；劝告；通知；提供意见

derivatives.zh: 同源名词，义为「建议」，以 c 结尾
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「顾问」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「明智的」
由本词加 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；公告」

senses.title: To recommend or counsel
senses.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人在某种情况下你认为他应当怎么做
senses.example: Her manager advised her to listen before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 经理建议她先听完再回答。
senses.why: The Old French source meant to give an opinion, and a opinion directed at action becomes a recommendation.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为「给出意见」，而针对行动的意见就成为建议。

senses.title: To inform formally
senses.definition: to give someone official or formal information about something
senses.definitionCN: 就某事向某人提供正式或官方的信息
senses.example: Please advise us of any change in your address.
senses.exampleCN: 地址如有变动，请通知我们。
senses.why: Giving notice was the older sense of the word, and business and law still use it.
senses.whyCN: 发出通知是这个词较老的意思，商业与法律至今仍这样用。

senses.title: To give professional guidance
senses.definition: to offer expert guidance in a field such as law, medicine, or finance
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、医学或金融等领域提供专家指导
senses.example: A lawyer advised the family on the will.
senses.exampleCN: 一位律师就遗嘱向这家人提供意见。
senses.why: Professionals turn their knowledge toward a client's problem, which is advising in the fullest sense.
senses.whyCN: 专业人士把自己的知识转向客户的问题，这就是最完整意义上的 advise。

senses.title: To counsel a client in law
senses.definition: in legal contexts, to counsel or represent a client's interests
senses.definitionCN: 在法律语境中，为当事人的利益提供咨询或代理
senses.example: Counsel advised the accused before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 律师在听证前为被告提供了法律意见。
senses.why: Law separates the professional who advises from the court that decides, and the verb marks that role.
senses.whyCN: 法律把提供意见的专业人士与作出裁决的法庭分开，这个动词标出前者的角色。

intro.en: Advise and advice are the verb and noun of one Old French word for opinion.
intro.cn: advise 与 advice 是同一个古法语「意见」词的动词与名词形式。

items.en: Videre meant to see.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」。

items.en: Visum meant seen, hence something that seems good.
items.cn: visum 意为「所见的」，因此指觉得好的东西。

items.en: Avis meant opinion or view.
items.cn: avis 意为意见或看法。

items.en: Aviser meant to give an opinion or to notice.
items.cn: aviser 意为给出意见或告知。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Everyday use kept recommending, while business and law kept formal informing.
items.cn: 日常用法保留「建议」，商业与法律保留「正式通知」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advice and advise pair again; the near-meaning group gathers recommending and informing verbs.
note.cn: 形近组再次对照 advice 与 advise；近义组收建议与告知类动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an opinion about what to do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「建议」，以 c 结尾，是 advise 的同源名词。

entries.definition: Worth recommending; sensible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的」，由本词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A person who gives advice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顾问」，由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Giving advice but not making decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「咨询的；公告」，由本词加 -ory 构成。

entries.definition: To say that something is good and should be chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推荐」，强调认为某物好。

entries.definition: To give serious or professional advice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「提供专业忠告」，语气正式。

entries.definition: To give someone facts or official information.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「通知、告知」，对应正式通知义项。

entries.definition: To put an idea forward for consideration.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提议」，语气比 advise 轻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the opinion root and the spelling split between the verb and the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「意见」词根，以及动词与名词之间的拼写分工。

normal.en: Avis means opinion, so advise is to give someone your opinion about action.
normal.cn: avis 意为意见，所以 advise 就是就行动向他人给出你的意见。

normal.en: Advise is the verb with s; advice is the noun with c.
normal.cn: advise 是以 s 结尾的动词，advice 是以 c 结尾的名词。

normal.en: Advise somebody to do is the standard pattern for a recommendation.
normal.cn: advise somebody to do 是表达建议的标准搭配。

normal.en: Advise against is the opposite: tell someone not to do it.
normal.cn: advise against 则是反面：劝人不要做。

normal.en: In business, please advise us means please tell us officially.
normal.cn: 在商业中，please advise us 意为请正式通知我们。

abstract.en: An old doctor leaning down to explain a dose.
abstract.cn: 一位老医生俯下身来说明用药剂量。

abstract.en: A hand pointing at one of two doors.
abstract.cn: 一只手指向两扇门中的一扇。

abstract.en: A letter of notice arriving before the event.
abstract.cn: 一封在事件之前到达的通知信。

examples.en: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.
examples.cn: 医生建议他休息一周。

examples.en: We advise against travelling tonight.
examples.cn: 我们劝你们今晚不要出行。

examples.en: Please advise us when the goods arrive.
examples.cn: 货物到达时请通知我们。

root: 经古法语 aviser「给出意见、告知」进入英语，根源是拉丁语 videre「看」及其分词 visum「所见的」。核心是「看过之后给出意见」，由此发展出「建议」「劝告」「正式通知」「专业意见」等义。注意动词 advise 以 s 结尾，名词 advice 以 c 结尾。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: recommending, informing formally, giving professional guidance, and counselling a legal client.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：建议、正式通知、提供专业意见、为法律当事人提供意见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an experienced doctor leans down to explain how to take a medicine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位有经验的医生俯身说明该怎样服药。

branches.en: THE ACTION: an opinion is turned toward what someone should do.
branches.cn: 行动线：意见被转向某人该做什么。

branches.en: THE NOTICE: the older sense of informing survives in business.
branches.cn: 通知线：较老的「告知」义在商业中保留。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: expert knowledge is applied to a client's problem.
branches.cn: 专业线：专家知识被用于客户的问题。

branches.en: THE COURT: legal advice is a formal professional role.
branches.cn: 法庭线：法律意见是一种正式的职业角色。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: whether a recommendation or a notice, words are sent to another person.
branches.cn: 信息线：无论建议还是通知，都是把话语送给他人。

senses.title: To publicly support a cause or policy
senses.definition: to speak or act publicly in support of a cause, policy, or group
senses.definitionCN: 公开以言语或行动支持某项事业、政策或群体
senses.example: Several doctors advocate a shorter working week.
senses.exampleCN: 几位医生主张缩短每周工作时间。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to call someone to one's aid, so advocating is calling support toward a cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「召人来帮忙」，所以提倡就是把支持召唤到某项事业上。

senses.title: A person who supports a cause
senses.definition: a person who publicly speaks or works for a cause or for the interests of a group
senses.definitionCN: 公开为某项事业或某群体利益发声、奔走的人
senses.example: She became an advocate for the old library and spoke at every meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了老图书馆的倡导者，并在每次会上发言。
senses.why: The noun is the person who has been called, or who calls others, to the aid of a cause.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指被召唤来、或召唤他人来支援某项事业的人。

senses.title: A lawyer who speaks for a client
senses.definition: a lawyer who pleads a client's case, especially in some legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 为当事人辩护的律师，尤用于某些法律体系
senses.example: The advocate rose to address the court.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师起身向法庭陈词。
senses.why: In law the advocate is literally the one called to a person's side to speak for them.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，辩护律师字面上就是被召到当事人身旁替其说话的人。

intro.en: Advocate comes from a Latin verb meaning to call someone to one's aid.
intro.cn: advocate 出自一个意为「召人来帮忙」的拉丁动词。

items.en: Vocare meant to call or summon.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼唤、召唤。

items.en: Ad- plus vocare gave 'to call to one's aid or support'.
items.cn: ad- 加 vocare 构成「召来相助或支持」。

items.en: Advocatus named a person called to help, especially in legal matters.
items.cn: advocatus 指被召来帮忙的人，尤指法律事务中的人。

items.en: Old French carried the noun and its legal sense toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词及其法律义带入英语。

items.en: The word is recorded in English in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪见于英语记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The legal sense narrowed, while the general sense of public support widened.
items.cn: 法律义收窄，而公开支持的一般义扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the 'call to aid' root; the near-meaning group gathers supporters and legal speakers.
note.cn: 形近组共享「召来相助」词根；近义组收支持者与法律代言人。

entries.definition: Public support for a cause or policy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倡导；拥护」，由本词加 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: A person who advocates; rarer than advocate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提倡者」，比 advocate 更少见。

entries.definition: Relating to advocacy; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「倡导的」，较罕见。

entries.definition: A hobby or secondary occupation; from the same verb of calling away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「业余爱好」，出自同一「召唤」动词，但语义分叉不同。

entries.definition: A person who backs a person, team, or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支持者」，范围最广。

entries.definition: A person who actively defends a cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「捍卫者；为……而战」，语气更强。

entries.definition: A person who helps something become accepted or successful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推动者、发起人」，侧重促成。

entries.definition: A person trained to advise clients and represent them in law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「律师」，对应法律义项的上位词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the 'call to aid' root from a courtroom to a community meeting.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「召来相助」词根，从法庭走到社区会议。

normal.en: Vocare means to call, so an advocate is someone called to help a cause.
normal.cn: vocare 意为召唤，所以 advocate 就是被召来帮助某项事业的人。

normal.en: Advocacy is the noun for the activity of advocating.
normal.cn: advocacy 是表示「倡导活动」的名词。

normal.en: A lawyer is called to a client's side, which is why advocate also means lawyer.
normal.cn: 律师被召到当事人身旁，所以 advocate 也指律师。

normal.en: Advocate for a cause is the modern way to say speak up for it.
normal.cn: advocate for a cause 是「为某项事业发声」的现代说法。

normal.en: A devil's advocate argues the other side just to test an idea.
normal.cn: devil's advocate 指为了检验观点而故意唱反调的人。

abstract.en: A figure standing in front of a crowd, one hand raised.
abstract.cn: 一个人站在人群前，举起一只手。

abstract.en: A voice lent to someone who has none.
abstract.cn: 把声音借给没有声音的人。

abstract.en: A chair pulled up beside the accused in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 法庭上，一把椅子被拉到被告身旁。

examples.en: The group advocates cleaner public transport.
examples.cn: 这个团体主张更清洁的公共交通。

examples.en: She is a strong advocate of free education.
examples.cn: 她是免费教育的坚定拥护者。

examples.en: The advocate presented the client's case calmly.
examples.cn: 辩护律师冷静地陈述了当事人的案情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃凯特」——阿德把大家召来，为无声者说话

root: 源自拉丁语 advocatus「被召来相助的人」，出自 advocare「召来相助」，由 ad-「向」加 vocare「召唤」构成；古法语 avocat 带入英语。核心是「被召到某人身边替他说话」，由此发展出「提倡、主张」「拥护者、倡导者」与「辩护律师」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: publicly supporting a cause, the person who supports it, and the lawyer who speaks for a client.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：公开支持某项事业、支持该事业的人、替当事人说话的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stands before a crowd with one hand raised, speaking for the voiceless.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在人群前举手，替无声者说话。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: support is called toward a policy or group.
branches.cn: 事业线：支持被召唤到某项政策或群体上。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the one who answers the call and speaks.
branches.cn: 人物线：回应召唤并开口说话的人。

branches.en: THE COURT: a lawyer is called to a client's side.
branches.cn: 法庭线：律师被召到当事人身旁。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the cause and its supporter share one act of speaking up.
branches.cn: 声音线：事业与支持者共享同一个「发声」动作。

branches.en: THE ROLE: supporter and lawyer are both called to help another.
branches.cn: 角色线：支持者与律师都是被召来帮助他人的。

intro.en: Advocate is a Latin verb of calling, with a person suffix and English endings around it.
intro.cn: advocate 是一个表示「召唤」的拉丁动词，带表示人的后缀，并加上英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, advocare and advocatus are recorded, so the family is well attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare、advocare 与 advocatus 均有记录，词族文献充分。

items.exampleCN: 它是 advocate 的直接来源。

items.example: It marks both noun and verb uses in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语中同时标出名词与动词用法。
